Man sabbaḥa-llāha fī duburi kulli ṣalātin thalāthan wa-thalāthīn
Thirty-three times declaring Allāh free of every fault, at the close of each prayer.
سَبَّحَ — root س ب ح. Tasbīḥ is clearing Allāh of anything unfitting. It comes first because denial precedes praise.
وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ ثَلَاثاً وَثَلَاثِينَ. وَكَبَّرَ اللَّهَ ثَلَاثاً وَثَلَاثِينَ.
wa-ḥamida-llāha thalāthan wa-thalāthīn, wa-kabbara-llāha thalāthan wa-thalāthīn
Then thirty-three of praise, then thirty-three of declaring Him greater.
وَكَبَّرَ — root ك ب ر. Form II kabbara means to call something great, not to make it great. The greatness is reported, not conferred.
فَتِلْكَ تِسْعَةٌ وَتِسْعُونَ، وَقَالَ تَمَامَ المِئَةِ:
fa-tilka tisʿatun wa-tisʿūn, wa-qāla tamāma-l-miʾah
The count is spelled out, and one sentence is left to round it off.
تَمَامَ — root ت م م. Tamām is the completing portion. The hundredth is not an extra but the piece that finishes the set.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ،
Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah
The hundredth place is given to the statement of tawḥīd.
شَرِيكَ — root ش ر ك. Sharīk is a business partner, someone with a share. Denying Him one denies any share in ownership or worship.
لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ.
lahu-l-mulku wa-lahu-l-ḥamd, wa-huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr
Ownership, praise and power named once more as the set closes.
المُلْكُ — root م ل ك. Al-mulk carries the definite article, so it is all dominion, not a share of it.
غُفِرَتْ خَطَايَاهُ؛ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ البَحْرِ
Ghufirat khaṭāyāh; wa-in kānat mithla zabadi-l-baḥr
The reward is stated plainly, with no ceiling put on the quantity forgiven.
زَبَدِ — root ز ب د. The book glosses zabad al-baḥr as what rises on the surface of the sea when it churns: countless, and light enough to be swept away.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
زَبَدِ البَحْرِزَبَدُ البَحْرِ: مَا يَعْلُو مَاءَ البَحْرِ عِنْدَ هَيَجَانِهِ
zabad al-baḥr — the foam of the seaZabad al-baḥr: what rises above the water of the sea when it is turbulent.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

٦
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ قَرَأَ آيَةَ الكُرْسِيِّ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ؛ لَمْ يَمْنَعْهُ مِنْ دُخُولِ الجَنَّةِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَمُوتَ»

↪ Recite Āyat al-Kursī (al-Baqarah 255) after each obligatory prayer.

✎Added by us

“Whoever recites Āyat al-Kursī at the end of every obligatory prayer, nothing keeps him from entering Paradise except that he must die first.”

Man qaraʾa āyata-l-kursiyyi fī duburi kulli ṣalātin maktūbah; lam yamnaʿhu min dukhūli-l-jannati illā an yamūt

مَنْ قَرَأَ آيَةَ الكُرْسِيِّ
Man qaraʾa āyata-l-kursiyy
One named verse, recited by whoever chooses to.
الكُرْسِيِّ — root ك ر س. Al-Kursī is the Footstool mentioned in the verse; the verse takes its name from the word inside it.
فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ؛
fī duburi kulli ṣalātin maktūbah
The five obligatory prayers, each one, not the voluntary ones.
مَكْتُوبَةٍ — root ك ت ب. Maktūbah means written down as a duty. It narrows kulli ṣalāh to the farḍ prayers.
لَمْ يَمْنَعْهُ مِنْ دُخُولِ الجَنَّةِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَمُوتَ
lam yamnaʿhu min dukhūli-l-jannati illā an yamūt
The only thing standing between him and Paradise is that he has not died yet.
يَمْنَعْهُ — root م ن ع. The negation plus illā makes death the single remaining obstacle, which is a promise dressed as a restriction.

رَوَاهُ النَّسَائِيُّ فِي السُّنَنِ الكُبْرَىReported by al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā

عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ عَامِرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir (may Allāh be pleased with him) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«أَمَرَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ بِالمُعَوِّذَاتِ دُبُرَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ»

↪ Recite Sūrat al-Falaq and Sūrat an-Nās after every prayer.

✎Added by us

ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, may Allāh be pleased with him, said: “The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ ordered me to recite the muʿawwidhāt at the end of every prayer.”

Amaranī rasūlu-llāhi ﷺ an aqraʾa bi-l-muʿawwidhāti dubura kulli ṣalāh

أَمَرَنِيhe ordered me
رَسُولُ اللَّهِthe Messenger of Allāh

بِالمُعَوِّذَاتِthe sūrahs of refuge
دُبُرَat the end of

صَلَاةٍprayer
أَمَرَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ
Amaranī rasūlu-llāhi ﷺ
This is a command he received, not a habit he noticed.
أَمَرَنِي — root أ م ر. Amara is an order. ʿUqbah reports the instruction itself, which is why the practice is not optional decoration.
أَنْ أَقْرَأَ بِالمُعَوِّذَاتِ
an aqraʾa bi-l-muʿawwidhāti
The thing commanded is recitation of the sūrahs of seeking refuge.
بِالمُعَوِّذَاتِ — root ع و ذ. The book identifies them as two: Qul aʿūdhu bi-rabbi-l-falaq and Qul aʿūdhu bi-rabbi-n-nās.
دُبُرَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ
dubura kulli ṣalāh
Directly after each prayer, with no prayer excluded.
دُبُرَ — root د ب ر. Here dubura is an adverb of place in time: on the heel of the prayer.
الكِتَابFrom the book

bi-l-muʿawwidhāt — with the sūrahs of refugeAnd they are two: the sūrah «Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak», and the sūrah «Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind».

رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُReported by Aḥmad

💎 الفَائِدَة · Deeper lesson
The prayer ends the way a careful worker ends a task — by seeking forgiveness for any shortcoming in it (three times), then declaring that Allah Himself is as-Salām, Peace. You leave the prayer having handed its flaws to the One who forgives.
⭐ Forgiven like the foam of the sea
The set of 33 + 33 + 33 (tasbīḥ, taḥmīd, takbīr) completed to a hundred with the tahlīl is one of the great bargains of the day: sins forgiven though they be like the foam of the sea. And Āyat al-Kursī after every obligatory prayer — only death stands between its reciter and Paradise.
✍️ Activityنَشَاط
After each obligatory prayer this week, go through the set in order: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ ×3, then اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلَامُ…, the 33/33/33 with the tahlīl to complete a hundred, Āyat al-Kursī, and the Muʿawwidhāt.

دُعَاءُ القُنُوتِ

Chapter 18 — The Duʿāʾ of Qunūt

Book p.50 · الصَّلَاةُ — The Prayer · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ الحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَاal-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (may Allāh be pleased with them both) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«عَلَّمَنِي النَّبِيُّ ﷺ كَلِمَاتٍ أَقُولُهُنَّ فِي الوِتْرِ: اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنِي فِيمَنْ هَدَيْتَ، وَعَافِنِي فِيمَنْ عَافَيْتَ. وَتَوَلَّنِي فِيمَنْ تَوَلَّيْتَ، وَبَارِكْ لِي فِيمَا أَعْطَيْتَ. وَقِنِي شَرَّ مَا قَضَيْتَ؛ فَإِنَّكَ تَقْضِي وَلَا يُقْضَى عَلَيْكَ. وَإِنَّهُ لَا يَذِلُّ مَنْ وَالَيْتَ، تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا وَتَعَالَيْتَ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay standing in qunūt, in the witr prayer.
اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنِي فِيمَنْ هَدَيْتَ، وَعَافِنِي فِيمَنْ عَافَيْتَ. وَتَوَلَّنِي فِيمَنْ تَوَلَّيْتَ، وَبَارِكْ لِي فِيمَا أَعْطَيْتَ. وَقِنِي شَرَّ مَا قَضَيْتَ؛ فَإِنَّكَ تَقْضِي وَلَا يُقْضَى عَلَيْكَ. وَإِنَّهُ لَا يَذِلُّ مَنْ وَالَيْتَ، تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا وَتَعَالَيْتَ
✎Added by us

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allāh be pleased with them both, said: “The Prophet ﷺ taught me words to say in witr: ‘O Allāh, guide me among those You have guided, keep me sound among those You have kept sound, take charge of me among those You have taken charge of, bless for me what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. You decree, and none decrees against You. No one You take as a friend is ever brought low. Blessed are You, our Lord, and exalted.’”

ʿAllamanī-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ kalimātin aqūluhunna fī-l-witr: Allāhumma-hdinī fīman hadayt, wa-ʿāfinī fīman ʿāfayt, wa-tawallanī fīman tawallayt, wa-bārik lī fīmā aʿṭayt, wa-qinī sharra mā qaḍayt; fa-innaka taqḍī wa-lā yuqḍā ʿalayk, wa-innahu lā yadhillu man wālayt, tabārakta rabbanā wa-taʿālayt

كَلِمَاتٍ — root ك ل م. Kalimāt, indefinite and plural, then the relative clause: words with a fixed place, said in witr.
اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنِي فِيمَنْ هَدَيْتَ، وَعَافِنِي فِيمَنْ عَافَيْتَ.
Allāhumma-hdinī fīman hadayt, wa-ʿāfinī fīman ʿāfayt
Ask to be placed inside a group Allāh has already guided and already kept whole.
فِيمَنْ — root none (compound of fī + man). Fīman means 'among those whom'. The request is for inclusion, which is humbler than asking on your own account.
وَتَوَلَّنِي فِيمَنْ تَوَلَّيْتَ، وَبَارِكْ لِي فِيمَا أَعْطَيْتَ.
wa-tawallanī fīman tawallayt, wa-bārik lī fīmā aʿṭayt
Ask Him to handle your affair Himself, and to put blessing into what He has already given.
وَتَوَلَّنِي — root و ل ي. The book glosses tawallanī as 'take charge of my affair'. It is more than help: it is management.
وَقِنِي شَرَّ مَا قَضَيْتَ؛
wa-qinī sharra mā qaḍayt
The decree is not objected to; protection is sought from the harm inside it.
وَقِنِي — root و ق ي. Qinī is a short imperative from waqā, to shield. Note what is asked against: the sharr of the decree, not the decree.
فَإِنَّكَ تَقْضِي وَلَا يُقْضَى عَلَيْكَ.
fa-innaka taqḍī wa-lā yuqḍā ʿalayk
The reason the request goes to Him: judgement runs one way only.
يُقْضَى — root ق ض ي. Yuqḍā is passive. The active and the passive of the same verb, set side by side, mark the difference between Him and everyone else.
وَإِنَّهُ لَا يَذِلُّ مَنْ وَالَيْتَ، تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا وَتَعَالَيْتَ
wa-innahu lā yadhillu man wālayt, tabārakta rabbanā wa-taʿālayt
His friendship is a shelter from disgrace, and the duʿāʾ closes with praise, not a request.
يَذِلُّ — root ذ ل ل. Dhull is the lowness of being abandoned. Set against wālayt from و ل ي, it draws the line between the befriended and the left alone.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
وَتَوَلَّنِيأَيْ: تَوَلَّ أَمْرِي
wa-tawallanī — and take charge of meThat is: take charge of my affair.

Book p.51 · الصَّلَاةُ — The Prayer · 1 entry in the printed text.

كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا سَلَّمَ مِنَ الوِتْرِ قَالَWhen the Prophet ﷺ gave the salām at the end of the witr he would say
الكِتَابFrom the book

«سُبْحَانَ المَلِكِ القُدُّوسِ - ثَلَاثاً -، وَيَرْفَعُ صَوْتَهُ بِالثَّالِثَةِ»

ثَلَاثاًthree times

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay three times after the salām of witr, aloud on the third.
سُبْحَانَ المَلِكِ القُدُّوسِ
✎Added by us

“Glory be to the King, the Most Holy” — three times — and he would raise his voice on the third.

Subḥāna-l-maliki-l-quddūs — thalāthan —, wa-yarfaʿu ṣawtahu bi-th-thālithah

سُبْحَانَglory be to
المَلِكِthe King
القُدُّوسِthe Most Holy
ثَلَاثاًthree times
وَيَرْفَعُand he raises
صَوْتَهُhis voice

سُبْحَانَ المَلِكِ القُدُّوسِ - ثَلَاثاً -،
Subḥāna-l-maliki-l-quddūs — thalāthan —
Two names together: the One who commands, and the One utterly pure.
القُدُّوسِ — root ق د س. Quddūs is an intensive form: purity that has no trace of the opposite in it. Coupled with al-Malik, it is authority without stain.
وَيَرْفَعُ صَوْتَهُ بِالثَّالِثَةِ
wa-yarfaʿu ṣawtahu bi-th-thālithah
The last of the three is said out loud, so the night ends on something audible.
وَيَرْفَعُ — root ر ف ع. The verb is imperfect, describing a habit he kept, not a single occasion.

الاِسْتِخَارَةُ

Chapter 20 — Seeking the Better Choice (Istikhārah)

Book p.52 · الصَّلَاةُ — The Prayer · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَJābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh (may Allāh be pleased with him) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يُعَلِّمُنَا الاِسْتِخَارَةَ فِي الأُمُورِ كُلِّهَا، كَمَا يُعَلِّمُنَا السُّورَةَ مِنَ القُرْآنِ. يَقُولُ: إِذَا هَمَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بِالأَمْرِ، فَلْيَرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ غَيْرِ الفَرِيضَةِ، ثُمَّ لْيَقُلْ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ العَظِيمِ. فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الغُيُوبِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي - أَوْ قَالَ: عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ -؛ فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي، وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي، ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ. وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي - أَوْ قَالَ: فِي عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ -؛ فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي، وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ، ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ. قَالَ: وَيُسَمِّي حَاجَتَهُ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْPray two rakʿahs outside the obligatory prayers, then say this, naming the matter you are deciding.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ العَظِيمِ. فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الغُيُوبِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي - أَوْ قَالَ: عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ -؛ فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي، وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي، ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ. وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي - أَوْ قَالَ: فِي عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ -؛ فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي، وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ، ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ
✎Added by us

Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, may Allāh be pleased with him, said: The Prophet ﷺ used to teach us istikhārah in all matters, as he taught us a sūrah of the Qurʾān. He would say: “When one of you has set his mind on something, let him pray two rakʿahs apart from the obligatory prayer, then let him say: ‘O Allāh, I ask You to choose for me by Your knowledge, and I ask You for capability by Your power, and I ask You out of Your immense bounty. You are able and I am not, You know and I do not, and You know all that is hidden. O Allāh, if You know this matter to be good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair — or he said: the near and the far of my affair — then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and then bless me in it. And if You know this matter to be bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair — or he said: in the near and the far of my affair — then turn it away from me, and turn me away from it, and decree for me what is good wherever it may be, and then make me content with it.’” He said: and he names the thing he needs.

Kāna-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ yuʿallimunā-l-istikhārata fī-l-umūri kullihā, kamā yuʿallimunā-s-sūrata mina-l-Qurʾān. Yaqūl: Idhā hamma aḥadukum bi-l-amr, fal-yarkaʿ rakʿatayni min ghayri-l-farīḍah, thumma l-yaqul: Allāhumma innī astakhīruka bi-ʿilmik, wa-astaqdiruka bi-qudratik, wa-asʾaluka min faḍlika-l-ʿaẓīm. Fa-innaka taqdiru wa-lā aqdir, wa-taʿlamu wa-lā aʿlam, wa-anta ʿallāmu-l-ghuyūb. Allāhumma in kunta taʿlamu anna hādhā-l-amra khayrun lī fī dīnī wa-maʿāshī wa-ʿāqibati amrī — aw qāla: ʿājili amrī wa-ājilih —; fa-qdurhu lī, wa-yassirhu lī, thumma bārik lī fīh. Wa-in kunta taʿlamu anna hādhā-l-amra sharrun lī fī dīnī wa-maʿāshī wa-ʿāqibati amrī — aw qāla: fī ʿājili amrī wa-ājilih —; fa-ṣrifhu ʿannī, wa-ṣrifnī ʿanh, wa-qdur liya-l-khayra ḥaythu kān, thumma arḍinī bih. Qāla: wa-yusammī ḥājatah

كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يُعَلِّمُنَا الاِسْتِخَارَةَ فِي الأُمُورِ كُلِّهَا، كَمَا يُعَلِّمُنَا السُّورَةَ مِنَ القُرْآنِ.
Kāna-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ yuʿallimunā-l-istikhārata fī-l-umūri kullihā, kamā yuʿallimunā-s-sūrata mina-l-Qurʾān
He taught this the way he taught Qurʾān: word for word, for every kind of decision.
الاِسْتِخَارَةَ — root خ ي ر. The book glosses istikhārah as asking for the better of two options. Form X: seeking, not being told.
يَقُولُ: إِذَا هَمَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بِالأَمْرِ، فَلْيَرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ غَيْرِ الفَرِيضَةِ، ثُمَّ لْيَقُلْ:
Yaqūl: Idhā hamma aḥadukum bi-l-amr, fal-yarkaʿ rakʿatayni min ghayri-l-farīḍah, thumma l-yaqul
Two units of prayer come before the words, and they must be voluntary ones.
هَمَّ — root ه م م. The book glosses hamma bi-l-amr as having formed an intention towards something. You are already leaning, and now you ask.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ العَظِيمِ.
Allāhumma innī astakhīruka bi-ʿilmik, wa-astaqdiruka bi-qudratik, wa-asʾaluka min faḍlika-l-ʿaẓīm
Three requests, each leaning on something of His: His knowledge, His power, His bounty.
وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ — root ق د ر. The book glosses astaqdiruka as asking Him to grant you the power to act. You are not asking for information only.
فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الغُيُوبِ.
Fa-innaka taqdiru wa-lā aqdir, wa-taʿlamu wa-lā aʿlam, wa-anta ʿallāmu-l-ghuyūb
The reason for asking, stated as a plain contrast in power and knowledge.
عَلَّامُ — root ع ل م. ʿAllām is the intensive of ʿālim: not one who knows, but one whose knowing has no limit. Ghuyūb is the plural of what is unseen.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي - أَوْ قَالَ: عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ -؛ فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي، وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي، ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ.
Allāhumma in kunta taʿlamu anna hādhā-l-amra khayrun lī fī dīnī wa-maʿāshī wa-ʿāqibati amrī — aw qāla: ʿājili amrī wa-ājilih —; fa-qdurhu lī, wa-yassirhu lī, thumma bārik lī fīh
If it is good, ask for three things in order: that it happen, that it be easy, that it be blessed.
وَعَاقِبَةِ — root ع ق ب. ʿĀqibah is what comes at the heel of a thing. Religion, living, and ending: the three places where a decision lands.
وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي - أَوْ قَالَ: فِي عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ -؛ فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي، وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ، ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ. قَالَ: وَيُسَمِّي حَاجَتَهُ
Wa-in kunta taʿlamu anna hādhā-l-amra sharrun lī fī dīnī wa-maʿāshī wa-ʿāqibati amrī — aw qāla: fī ʿājili amrī wa-ājilih —; fa-ṣrifhu ʿannī, wa-ṣrifnī ʿanh, wa-qdur liya-l-khayra ḥaythu kān, thumma arḍinī bih. Qāla: wa-yusammī ḥājatah
If it is bad, ask for it to be moved away, for you to be moved away, and for contentment with whatever comes instead.
أَرْضِنِي — root ر ض ي. The last request is about the heart, not the outcome. The book adds that the person names his actual need inside the duʿāʾ.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
الاِسْتِخَارَةَأَيْ: طَلَبَ خَيْرِ الأَمْرَيْنِ
al-istikhārah — seeking the better choiceThat is: seeking the better of the two matters.
بِالأَمْرِأَيْ: قَصَدَ أَمْراً
bi-l-amr — concerning a matterThat is: he intended some matter.

Workbook — what to do and say when you feel a pain anywhere in your body.

When

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
✎Added by us

ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, may Allāh be pleased with him, complained to the Prophet ﷺ of a pain he had been feeling in his body since he became Muslim. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Put your hand on the part of your body that hurts and say ‘Bismi-llāh’ three times. Then say seven times: ‘I seek refuge in Allāh and in His power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear.’”

Annahu shakā ilā-n-Nabiyyi ﷺ wajaʿan yajiduhu fī jasadihi mundhu aslam, fa-qāla lahu-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ: Daʿ yadaka ʿalā-lladhī taʾallama min jasadik, wa-qul: Bismi-llāh — thalāthan —. Wa-qul — sabʿa marrāt —: Aʿūdhu bi-llāhi wa-qudratihi min sharri mā ajidu wa-uḥādhir

أَنَّهُ شَكَا إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَجَعاً يَجِدُهُ فِي جَسَدِهِ مُنْذُ أَسْلَمَ،
Annahu shakā ilā-n-Nabiyyi ﷺ wajaʿan yajiduhu fī jasadihi mundhu aslam
A long-standing pain, carried since the day he entered Islam, brought to the Prophet ﷺ.
مُنْذُ — root none (particle). Mundhu marks the start point. The pain is not new, which is why the remedy is a practice rather than a one-off.
فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: ضَعْ يَدَكَ عَلَى الَّذِي تَأَلَّمَ مِنْ جَسَدِكَ،
fa-qāla lahu-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ: Daʿ yadaka ʿalā-lladhī taʾallama min jasadik
The treatment begins with the hand placed on the exact spot that hurts.
تَأَلَّمَ — root أ ل م. Taʾallama is Form V: to be in pain. The hand goes on the place itself, not on the body in general.
وَقُلْ: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ - ثَلَاثاً -.
wa-qul: Bismi-llāh — thalāthan —
Three times, the name of Allāh over the place.
وَقُلْ — root ق و ل. The imperative is bare: say it, out loud, while the hand rests there.
وَقُلْ - سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ -:
Wa-qul — sabʿa marrāt —
Then a second formula, this time seven times.
مَرَّاتٍ — root م ر ر. Marrāt is the plural of marrah, one instance. The counts are part of the instruction, not decoration.
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ وَأُحَاذِرُ
Aʿūdhu bi-llāhi wa-qudratihi min sharri mā ajidu wa-uḥādhir
Refuge is sought from two things: the pain being felt now, and the harm feared next.
وَأُحَاذِرُ — root ح ذ ر. The book glosses uḥādhir as what I take precautions against. Ajidu is the present pain; uḥādhir is the dread of worse.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
وَأُحَاذِرُأَيْ: مَا أَحْذَرُ مِنْهُ
wa-uḥādhiru — and I am wary ofThat is: that which I am on guard against.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

💎 الفَائِدَة · Deeper lesson
Notice the two parts: a hand on the pain and words on the tongue. You take the practical step and hand the outcome to Allah — seeking refuge in His power from both what you already feel and what you fear may come.
✍️ Activityنَشَاط
Next time something aches, try the sunnah before anything else: hand on the spot, بِسْمِ اللَّهِ ×3, then أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ وَأُحَاذِرُ ×7.

“No harm. A cleansing, if Allāh wills.”

The first words out of his mouth settle the sick person rather than alarm him.
بَأْسَ — root ب أ س. Baʾs is harm or severity. Denying it is not a medical claim; it is reassurance about where this ends.

“O Allāh, Lord of mankind, take away the hardship. Heal him, for You are the Healer. There is no cure but Your cure — a cure that leaves no illness behind.”

Allāhumma rabba-n-nās, adhhibi-l-bās. Ishfihi wa-anta-sh-Shāfī, lā shifāʾa illā shifāʾuk, shifāʾan lā yughādiru saqaman

اللَّهُمَّO Allāh
رَبَّLord of
النَّاسِmankind
أَذْهِبِtake away
البَاسَthe hardship

وَأَنْتَand You are

لَاthere is no

اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، أَذْهِبِ البَاسَ.
Allāhumma rabba-n-nās, adhhibi-l-bās
He is addressed as Lord of all people, then asked to remove the distress.
البَاسَ — root ب أ س. The book glosses al-bās as ash-shiddah, the severity. Note the rhyme with an-nās: the wording is built to be easy to hold.
اشْفِهِ وَأَنْتَ الشَّافِي،
Ishfihi wa-anta-sh-Shāfī
The request and its reason in one breath: heal, because healing is Yours to do.
الشَّافِي — root ش ف ي. Ash-Shāfī with the article: the Healer, definite and exclusive. Medicine is a means; the healing is His.
لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاؤُكَ،
lā shifāʾa illā shifāʾuk
Every real cure is His cure, whatever hands it passes through.
شِفَاءَ — root ش ف ي. Shifāʾ is the cure itself. The negation with illā rules out any rival source before naming His.
شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَماً
shifāʾan lā yughādiru saqaman
Not partial relief: a cure that finishes the illness off completely.
سَقَماً — root س ق م. The book glosses it: leaving no illness behind. Saqam is chronic sickness, the kind that lingers after the worst has passed.

قُلْSay over someone who is ill.
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَرْقِيكَ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يُؤْذِيكَ. مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ أَوْ عَيْنِ حَاسِدٍ، اللَّهُ يَشْفِيكَ. بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَرْقِيكَ
✎Added by us

Jibrīl came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Muḥammad, are you ill?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “In the name of Allāh I recite over you, against everything that harms you, against the evil of every soul and every envious eye. May Allāh heal you. In the name of Allāh I recite over you.”

Yā Muḥammad, ashtakayt? Fa-qāla: Naʿam. Qāla: Bismi-llāhi arqīk, min kulli shayʾin yuʾdhīk. Min sharri kulli nafsin aw ʿayni ḥāsid, Allāhu yashfīk. Bismi-llāhi arqīk

أَوْor

يَشْفِيكَheals you
بِسْمِ اللَّهِin the name of Allāh
أَرْقِيكَI recite over you
يَا مُحَمَّدُ، اشْتَكَيْتَ؟ فَقَالَ: نَعَمْ. قَالَ:
Yā Muḥammad, ashtakayt? Fa-qāla: Naʿam. Qāla
A question first, and a plain answer: he was unwell, and said so.
اشْتَكَيْتَ — root ش ك و. The book glosses ashtakayt as 'have you fallen ill?'. The same root gives shakwā, a complaint: illness is something you voice.
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَرْقِيكَ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يُؤْذِيكَ.
Bismi-llāhi arqīk, min kulli shayʾin yuʾdhīk
The recitation opens with Allāh's name and covers anything that could hurt him.
أَرْقِيكَ — root ر ق ي. The book glosses arqīk as 'I seek refuge for you'. Ruqyah is treating by recitation, and it is done for someone, not at them.
مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ أَوْ عَيْنِ حَاسِدٍ،
Min sharri kulli nafsin aw ʿayni ḥāsid
Two named sources of harm: any person, and the eye of one who envies.
حَاسِدٍ — root ح س د. Ḥāsid is the active participle: the one doing the envying. The harm is traced to the envier, not to the eye by itself.
اللَّهُ يَشْفِيكَ. بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَرْقِيكَ
Allāhu yashfīk. Bismi-llāhi arqīk
The healing is placed with Allāh, and the opening line is repeated to close.
يَشْفِيكَ — root ش ف ي. Yashfīk is a statement, not a request: Allāh heals you. The repetition of bismi-llāhi arqīk frames the whole ruqyah.
الكِتَابFrom the book

اشْتَكَيْتَأَيْ: مَرِضْتَ؟
ishtakayta — you are ailingThat is: have you fallen ill?

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

٤
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ عَادَ مَرِيضاً لَمْ يَحْضُرْ أَجَلُهُ، فَقَالَ عِنْدَهُ - سَبْعَ مِرَارٍ -: أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ العَظِيمَ رَبَّ العَرْشِ العَظِيمِ أَنْ يَشْفِيَكَ؛ إِلَّا عَافَاهُ اللَّهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ المَرَضِ»

سَبْعَ مِرَارٍseven times

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay seven times beside the sick person.
أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ العَظِيمَ رَبَّ العَرْشِ العَظِيمِ أَنْ يَشْفِيَكَ
✎Added by us

“Whoever visits a sick person whose time has not yet come, and says beside him seven times: ‘I ask Allāh the Great, Lord of the Great Throne, to heal you’ — Allāh will cure him of that illness.”

Man ʿāda marīḍan lam yaḥḍur ajaluh, fa-qāla ʿindahu — sabʿa mirār —: Asʾalu-llāha-l-ʿaẓīma rabba-l-ʿarshi-l-ʿaẓīmi an yashfiyak; illā ʿāfāhu-llāhu min dhālika-l-maraḍ

المَرَضِillness
مَنْ عَادَ مَرِيضاً لَمْ يَحْضُرْ أَجَلُهُ،
Man ʿāda marīḍan lam yaḥḍur ajaluh
A visit to someone whose appointed term has not arrived; the promise is bounded by that.
أَجَلُهُ — root أ ج ل. Ajal is the fixed term of a life. The condition is honest: this duʿāʾ does not overturn a decreed death.
فَقَالَ عِنْدَهُ - سَبْعَ مِرَارٍ -:
fa-qāla ʿindahu — sabʿa mirār —
Said in his presence, seven times over.
عِنْدَهُ — root ع ن د. ʿIndahu places the speaker beside the sick person. Presence is part of the practice.
أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ العَظِيمَ رَبَّ العَرْشِ العَظِيمِ أَنْ يَشْفِيَكَ؛
Asʾalu-llāha-l-ʿaẓīma rabba-l-ʿarshi-l-ʿaẓīmi an yashfiyak
Allāh is called by greatness twice: in Himself, and as Lord of the greatest created thing.
العَظِيمَ — root ع ظ م. Al-ʿaẓīm appears twice, once for Allāh and once for the Throne. Asking big of the One who is great is part of the manners of duʿāʾ.
إِلَّا عَافَاهُ اللَّهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ المَرَضِ
illā ʿāfāhu-llāhu min dhālika-l-maraḍ
The answer is stated as a certainty, not a hope.
عَافَاهُ — root ع ف و. ʿĀfāhu means He restored him to soundness. Note the construction: a negative frame with illā, so the result is presented as inevitable.

رَوَاهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَReported by Abū Dāwūd

٥
كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذَا اشْتَكَى الإِنْسَانُ الشَّيْءَ مِنْهُ، أَوْ كَانَتْ بِهِ قَرْحَةٌ، أَوْ جُرْحٌ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ بِإِصْبَعِهِ هَكَذَا - وَوَضَعَ سَبَّابَتَهُ بِالأَرْضِ، ثُمَّ رَفَعَهَا -When a person complained of something ailing him, or had a sore or a wound, the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ would do thus with his finger - he placed his index finger on the ground, then raised it - and said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ، تُرْبَةُ أَرْضِنَا، بِرِيقَةِ بَعْضِنَا، لِيُشْفَى بِهِ سَقِيمُنَا، بِإِذْنِ رَبِّنَا»

↪ Say while wiping the sore place with a fingertip of moistened earth.

✎Added by us

“In the name of Allāh: the dust of our earth, with the saliva of one of us, that our sick one may be healed by it, by the permission of our Lord.”

Bi-ismi-llāh, turbatu arḍinā, bi-rīqati baʿḍinā, li-yushfā bihi saqīmunā, bi-idhni rabbinā

بِاسْمِin the name of
اللَّهِAllāh
تُرْبَةُthe dust of
أَرْضِنَاour earth
بِرِيقَةِwith the saliva of
بَعْضِنَاone of us
لِيُشْفَىso that may be healed
بِهِby it
سَقِيمُنَاour sick one
بِإِذْنِby the permission of
رَبِّنَاour Lord
بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ،
Bi-ismi-llāh
The action starts with His name, as every act of treatment does.
بِاسْمِ — root س م و. The book spells it here بِاسْمِ with the alif written, though it is read bismi-llāh. Same words as the other ruqyah, different orthography.
تُرْبَةُ أَرْضِنَا،
turbatu arḍinā
A little earth, taken from the ground under our feet.
تُرْبَةُ — root ت ر ب. Turbah is soil. The book explains the gesture: the fingertip is touched to the ground so that some of it clings.
بِرِيقَةِ بَعْضِنَا،
bi-rīqati baʿḍinā
Mixed with the saliva of one of us, so the dust holds together.
بِرِيقَةِ — root ر ي ق. Rīqah is a small amount of saliva. Baʿḍinā, 'one of us', keeps the wording communal rather than personal.
لِيُشْفَى بِهِ سَقِيمُنَا، بِإِذْنِ رَبِّنَا
li-yushfā bihi saqīmunā, bi-idhni rabbinā
The purpose is healing, and the last phrase hands the outcome back to Allāh.
بِإِذْنِ — root أ ذ ن. Idhn is permission. The dust and saliva are only a means; the book notes the words are said while wiping the wounded or ailing place.
الكِتَابFrom the book

قَرْحَةٌالقَرْحَةُ: مَا يَخْرُجُ عَلَى الأَعْضَاءِ مِثْلَ الدُّمَّلِ
qarḥah — a soreAl-qarḥah: what breaks out on the limbs, like a boil.
وَوَضَعَأَيِ: الرَّاوِي
wa-waḍaʿa — and he placedThat is: the narrator.
بِإِذْنِ رَبِّنَاأَيْ: أَنَّهُ يَأْخُذُ مِنْ رِيقِ نَفْسِهِ عَلَى إِصْبَعِهِ السَّبَّابَةِ. ثُمَّ يَضَعُهَا عَلَى التُّرَابِ، فَيَعْلَقُ بِهَا مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ. ثُمَّ يَمْسَحُ بِهِ عَلَى المَوْضِعِ الجَرِيحِ أَوِ العَلِيلِ، وَيَقُولُ حَالَ المَسْحِ: «بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ، تُرْبَةُ أَرْضِنَا ...»
bi-idhni rabbinā — by the permission of our LordThat is: he takes some of his own saliva on his index finger, then places it on the dust, so that something of it clings to the finger. Then he wipes it over the wounded or ailing spot, saying while wiping: “In the name of Allāh, the soil of our land …”

مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِAgreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

💎 الفَائِدَة · Deeper lesson
The first duʿāʾ reframes the whole illness: it is not a punishment but a ṭahūr — a washing-clean of sins. The second turns to the Lord of the Mighty Throne, the only One who can lift it. Together they comfort the heart and ask the cure from its true Source.
✍️ Activityنَشَاط
Learn the short one first — لَا بَأْسَ طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ — and say it the next time you visit or message someone who is unwell.

Chapter 23 — What the Dying Person Says

Book p.62 · المَرَضُ — Illness · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ كَانَ آخِرُ كَلَامِهِ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ؛ دَخَلَ الجَنَّةَ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْThe words to end on, and to prompt gently for someone who is dying.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
✎Added by us

“Whoever's last words are ‘There is no god but Allāh’ enters Paradise.”

Man kāna ākhiru kalāmihi: Lā ilāha illa-llāh; dakhala-l-jannah

مَنْwhoever
كَانَwas
آخِرُthe last of
كَلَامِهِhis speech
لَاno
إِلَهَgod
إِلَّاexcept
اللَّهُAllāh
دَخَلَhe entered
الجَنَّةَParadise
مَنْ كَانَ آخِرُ كَلَامِهِ:
Man kāna ākhiru kalāmihi
What counts here is the last thing said, not the amount said before it.
آخِرُ — root أ خ ر. Ākhir is the final one in a series. The condition is placed on the end of a life, which is why the habit is built long before.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ؛
Lā ilāha illa-llāh
The shahādah in its shortest form, the sentence to close on.
إِلَهَ — root أ ل ه. Ilāh is anything taken as an object of worship. The phrase clears them all away, then names the one that remains.
دَخَلَ الجَنَّةَ
dakhala-l-jannah
The consequence, stated in the past tense as something settled.
دَخَلَ — root د خ ل. The perfect verb is used for a future certainty, a common Arabic way of saying that the matter is already decided.

Chapter 24 — Supplication for the Deceased in the Funeral Prayer

Book p.64 · الجَنَازَةُ — The Funeral · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ عَوْفُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُʿAwf ibn Mālik (may Allāh be pleased with him) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«صَلَّى النَّبِيُّ ﷺ عَلَى جَنَازَةٍ، فَحَفِظْتُ مِنْ دُعَائِهِ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ، وَارْحَمْهُ، وَعَافِهِ، وَاعْفُ عَنْهُ. وَأَكْرِمْ نُزُلَهُ، وَوَسِّعْ مُدْخَلَهُ. وَاغْسِلْهُ بِالمَاءِ وَالثَّلْجِ وَالبَرَدِ. وَنَقِّهِ مِنَ الخَطَايَا كَمَا نَقَّيْتَ الثَّوْبَ الأَبْيَضَ مِنَ الدَّنَسِ. وَأَبْدِلْهُ دَاراً خَيْراً مِنْ دَارِهِ، وَأَهْلاً خَيْراً مِنْ أَهْلِهِ، وَزَوْجاً خَيْراً مِنْ زَوْجِهِ. وَأَدْخِلْهُ الجَنَّةَ، وَأَعِذْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ القَبْرِ، وَمِنْ عَذَابِ النَّارِ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay in the funeral prayer, as the supplication for the deceased.
اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ، وَارْحَمْهُ، وَعَافِهِ، وَاعْفُ عَنْهُ. وَأَكْرِمْ نُزُلَهُ، وَوَسِّعْ مُدْخَلَهُ. وَاغْسِلْهُ بِالمَاءِ وَالثَّلْجِ وَالبَرَدِ. وَنَقِّهِ مِنَ الخَطَايَا كَمَا نَقَّيْتَ الثَّوْبَ الأَبْيَضَ مِنَ الدَّنَسِ. وَأَبْدِلْهُ دَاراً خَيْراً مِنْ دَارِهِ، وَأَهْلاً خَيْراً مِنْ أَهْلِهِ، وَزَوْجاً خَيْراً مِنْ زَوْجِهِ. وَأَدْخِلْهُ الجَنَّةَ، وَأَعِذْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ القَبْرِ، وَمِنْ عَذَابِ النَّارِ
✎Added by us

The Prophet ﷺ prayed over a funeral, and I memorised from his supplication while he was saying: “O Allāh, forgive him, have mercy on him, grant him well-being, and pardon him. Honour his lodging, and widen his place of entry. Wash him with water, snow and hail. Cleanse him of his sins as You cleanse a white garment of filth. Give him a home better than his home, a family better than his family, and a spouse better than his spouse. Admit him to Paradise, and shelter him from the punishment of the grave and from the punishment of the Fire.”

Ṣallā-n-nabiyyu ﷺ ʿalā janāzatin, fa-ḥafiẓtu min duʿāʾihi wa-huwa yaqūl: Allāhumma-ghfir lahu, wa-rḥamhu, wa-ʿāfihi, wa-ʿfu ʿanhu. Wa-akrim nuzulahu, wa-wassiʿ mudkhalahu. Wa-ghsilhu bi-l-māʾi wa-th-thalji wa-l-barad. Wa-naqqihi mina-l-khaṭāyā kamā naqqayta-th-thawba-l-abyaḍa mina-d-danas. Wa-abdilhu dāran khayran min dārihi, wa-ahlan khayran min ahlihi, wa-zawjan khayran min zawjihi. Wa-adkhilhu-l-jannah, wa-aʿidhhu min ʿadhābi-l-qabri, wa-min ʿadhābi-n-nār.

صَلَّى النَّبِيُّ ﷺ عَلَى جَنَازَةٍ، فَحَفِظْتُ مِنْ دُعَائِهِ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ
Ṣallā-n-nabiyyu ﷺ ʿalā janāzatin, fa-ḥafiẓtu min duʿāʾihi wa-huwa yaqūl
ʿAwf stood in the prayer and kept the wording, so the duʿāʾ reaches us as it was said.
فَحَفِظْتُ — root ح ف ظ. Ḥafiẓtu is to preserve intact, not merely to recall the gist. The Companion is telling you why the words are exact.
اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ، وَارْحَمْهُ، وَعَافِهِ، وَاعْفُ عَنْهُ
Allāhumma-ghfir lahu, wa-rḥamhu, wa-ʿāfihi, wa-ʿfu ʿanhu
Four things asked at once: forgiveness, mercy, well-being, and pardon.
وَعَافِهِ — root ع ف و. ʿĀfihi asks for ʿāfiyah, soundness and relief. It is asked for the dead as it is for the living.
وَأَكْرِمْ نُزُلَهُ، وَوَسِّعْ مُدْخَلَهُ
wa-akrim nuzulahu, wa-wassiʿ mudkhalahu
He has arrived somewhere; ask that his reception be generous and his space wide.
نُزُلَهُ — root ن ز ل. The book glosses an-nuzul as what is prepared for a guest when he arrives. Mudkhalahu, the book says, means his grave.
وَاغْسِلْهُ بِالمَاءِ وَالثَّلْجِ وَالبَرَدِ. وَنَقِّهِ مِنَ الخَطَايَا كَمَا نَقَّيْتَ الثَّوْبَ الأَبْيَضَ مِنَ الدَّنَسِ
wa-ghsilhu bi-l-māʾi wa-th-thalji wa-l-barad, wa-naqqihi mina-l-khaṭāyā kamā naqqayta-th-thawba-l-abyaḍa mina-d-danas
Washing imagery: sins lifted off him the way dirt is lifted off white cloth.
وَنَقِّهِ — root ن ق ي. Naqqā is to leave a thing clean, not just wet. White cloth is chosen because nothing hides on it.
وَأَبْدِلْهُ دَاراً خَيْراً مِنْ دَارِهِ، وَأَهْلاً خَيْراً مِنْ أَهْلِهِ، وَزَوْجاً خَيْراً مِنْ زَوْجِهِ
wa-abdilhu dāran khayran min dārihi, wa-ahlan khayran min ahlihi, wa-zawjan khayran min zawjihi
Everything he left behind is asked for again, better: house, family, spouse.
وَأَبْدِلْهُ — root ب د ل. Abdil is exchange, one thing put in place of another. Not an addition to what he had, a replacement for it.
وَأَدْخِلْهُ الجَنَّةَ، وَأَعِذْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ القَبْرِ، وَمِنْ عَذَابِ النَّارِ
wa-adkhilhu-l-jannah, wa-aʿidhhu min ʿadhābi-l-qabri, wa-min ʿadhābi-n-nār
Close with the two things that matter now: entry to Paradise, safety from both punishments.
وَأَعِذْهُ — root ع و ذ. Aʿidhhu is to give shelter to someone fleeing. The grave is named before the Fire because it comes first.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
النُّزُلُمَا يُهَيَّأُ لِلضَّيْفِ عِنْدَ قُدُومِهِ
al-nuzul — provision for a guestWhat is prepared for a guest upon his arrival.
مُدْخَلَهُأَيْ: قَبْرُهُ
mudkhalahu — his place of entryThat is: his grave.

التَّعْزِيَةُ

Chapter 25 — Offering Condolence

Book p.66 · الجَنَازَةُ — The Funeral · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
عَنْ أُسَامَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَUsāmah ibn Zayd (may Allāh be pleased with them both) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كُنَّا عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَأَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِ إِحْدَى بَنَاتِهِ تَدْعُوهُ، وَتُخْبِرُهُ أَنَّ صَبِيّاً لَهَا فِي المَوْتِ. فَقَالَ لِلرَّسُولِ: ارْجِعْ إِلَيْهَا، فَأَخْبِرْهَا أَنَّ: لِلَّهِ مَا أَخَذَ، وَلَهُ مَا أَعْطَى، وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِأَجَلٍ مُسَمَّى؛ فَمُرْهَا: فَلْتَصْبِرْ وَلْتَحْتَسِبْ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay when consoling someone whose relative is dying or has died.
لِلَّهِ مَا أَخَذَ، وَلَهُ مَا أَعْطَى، وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِأَجَلٍ مُسَمَّى
✎Added by us

We were with the Prophet ﷺ when one of his daughters sent for him, calling him and telling him that a small son of hers was dying. He said to the messenger, “Go back to her and tell her: to Allāh belongs what He has taken, and to Him belongs what He has given, and everything with Him has an appointed term. And order her to be patient and to seek her reward.”

Kunnā ʿinda-n-nabiyyi ﷺ, fa-arsalat ilayhi iḥdā banātihi tadʿūhu, wa-tukhbiruhu anna ṣabiyyan lahā fī-l-mawt. Fa-qāla li-r-rasūl: irjiʿ ilayhā, fa-akhbirhā anna: li-llāhi mā akhadha, wa-lahu mā aʿṭā, wa-kullu shayʾin ʿindahu bi-ajalin musammā; fa-murhā: fa-l-taṣbir wa-l-taḥtasib.

إِلَيْهِto him

وَلْتَحْتَسِبْand let her seek the reward
كُنَّا عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَأَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِ إِحْدَى بَنَاتِهِ تَدْعُوهُ، وَتُخْبِرُهُ أَنَّ صَبِيّاً لَهَا فِي المَوْتِ
Kunnā ʿinda-n-nabiyyi ﷺ, fa-arsalat ilayhi iḥdā banātihi tadʿūhu, wa-tukhbiruhu anna ṣabiyyan lahā fī-l-mawt
A daughter sends word that her small son is dying, and asks him to come.
المَوْتِ — root م و ت. The book glosses fī-l-mawt as being in the onset of death. The child has not died yet.
فَقَالَ لِلرَّسُولِ: ارْجِعْ إِلَيْهَا، فَأَخْبِرْهَا أَنَّ
fa-qāla li-r-rasūl: irjiʿ ilayhā, fa-akhbirhā anna
He does not go; he sends words back, and the words are the point.
فَأَخْبِرْهَا — root خ ب ر. Akhbirhā is to convey information. What comforts her here is something true, not something soothing.
لِلَّهِ مَا أَخَذَ، وَلَهُ مَا أَعْطَى
li-llāhi mā akhadha, wa-lahu mā aʿṭā
The child was never hers to keep. Taking and giving are both His.
أَخَذَ — root أ خ ذ. Akhadha is put before aʿṭā so the loss is faced first, then placed where it belongs.
وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِأَجَلٍ مُسَمَّى
wa-kullu shayʾin ʿindahu bi-ajalin musammā
Nothing arrives early or late; each thing has a term already fixed.
بِأَجَلٍ — root أ ج ل. An ajal is a set end point, and musammā means named. The timing is not accidental.
فَمُرْهَا: فَلْتَصْبِرْ وَلْتَحْتَسِبْ
fa-murhā: fa-l-taṣbir wa-l-taḥtasib
Two instructions follow the belief: hold steady, and count on the reward.
وَلْتَحْتَسِبْ — root ح س ب. Iḥtasaba is to reckon something to your account with Allāh. Patience alone is endurance; iḥtisāb makes it worship.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
فِي المَوْتِأَيْ: فِي مُقَدِّمَاتِ المَوْتِ
fī al-mawt — in deathThat is: in the onset of death.

مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِAgreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

Chapter 26 — Supplication for the Deceased After Burial

Book p.67 · الجَنَازَةُ — The Funeral · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنْ دَفْنِ المَيِّتِ: وَقَفَ عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَWhen the Prophet ﷺ finished burying the deceased he would stand over him and say
الكِتَابFrom the book

«اسْتَغْفِرُوا لِأَخِيكُمْ، وَسَلُوا لَهُ التَّثْبِيتَ؛ فَإِنَّهُ الآنَ يُسْأَلُ»

✎Added by us

“Seek forgiveness for your brother, and ask that he be made firm, for he is being questioned right now.”

Istaghfirū li-akhīkum, wa-salū lahu-t-tathbīt; fa-innahu-l-āna yusʾal.

اسْتَغْفِرُواseek forgiveness
لِأَخِيكُمْfor your brother
وَسَلُواand ask
لَهُfor him
التَّثْبِيتَthe making firm
فَإِنَّهُfor indeed he
الآنَright now
يُسْأَلُis being questioned
اسْتَغْفِرُوا لِأَخِيكُمْ
Istaghfirū li-akhīkum
The first thing to do at a filled grave is ask forgiveness for the one in it.
اسْتَغْفِرُوا — root غ ف ر. Form X, so the asking is on his behalf. Brotherhood is named to make the duty personal.
وَسَلُوا لَهُ التَّثْبِيتَ
wa-salū lahu-t-tathbīt
Then ask that he hold steady, because he is about to be tested.
التَّثْبِيتَ — root ث ب ت. The book explains it: ask that he be made firm upon the correct answer.
فَإِنَّهُ الآنَ يُسْأَلُ
fa-innahu-l-āna yusʾal
The urgency is in the timing. The questioning is happening as you stand there.
يُسْأَلُ — root س أ ل. The book specifies the questions: about his Lord, his religion and his Prophet.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
وَقَفَ عَلَيْهِأَيْ: عِنْدَ القَبْرِ
waqafa ʿalayhi — he stood over himThat is: at the grave.
وَسَلُوا لَهُ التَّثْبِيتَ؛ فَإِنَّهُ الآنَ يُسْأَلُأَيْ: ادْعُوا لَهُ بِالتَّثْبِيتِ عَلَى الجَوَابِ الصَّوَابِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ الآنَ يُسْأَلُ عَنْ رَبِّهِ وَدِينِهِ وَنَبِيِّهِ
wa-salū lahu al-tathbīta — ask steadfastness for himThat is: supplicate for him to be made firm upon the correct answer, for he is now being questioned about his Lord, his religion, and his Prophet.

Chapter 27 — The Supplication for Visiting Graves

Book p.68 · الجَنَازَةُ — The Funeral · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
عَنْ بُرَيْدَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَBuraydah (may Allāh be pleased with him) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يُعَلِّمُهُمْ إِذَا خَرَجُوا إِلَى المَقَابِرِ: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيَارِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ وَالمُسْلِمِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَلَاحِقُونَ. أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ لَنَا وَلَكُمُ العَافِيَةَ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay on arriving at a graveyard.
السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيَارِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ وَالمُسْلِمِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَلَاحِقُونَ. أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ لَنَا وَلَكُمُ العَافِيَةَ
✎Added by us

The Prophet ﷺ used to teach them, when they went out to the graveyards, to say: “Peace be upon you, people of these dwellings, from among the believers and the Muslims. And we, if Allāh wills, are to follow you. I ask Allāh for well-being for us and for you.”

Kāna-n-nabiyyu ﷺ yuʿallimuhum idhā kharajū ilā-l-maqābir: as-salāmu ʿalaykum ahla-d-diyāri mina-l-muʾminīna wa-l-muslimīn, wa-innā in shāʾa-llāhu la-lāḥiqūn. Asʾalu-llāha lanā wa-lakumu-l-ʿāfiyah.

كَانَhe used to
النَّبِيُّthe Prophet
يُعَلِّمُهُمْteach them
إِذَاwhen
خَرَجُواthey went out
إِلَىto
المَقَابِرِthe graveyards
السَّلَامُpeace

أَهْلَO people of
الدِّيَارِthe dwellings
مِنَfrom among
المُؤْمِنِينَthe believers
وَالمُسْلِمِينَand the Muslims
وَإِنَّاand we
إِنْif
شَاءَwills
اللَّهُAllāh

أَسْأَلُI ask
اللَّهَAllāh
لَنَاfor us
وَلَكُمُand for you
العَافِيَةَwell-being
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يُعَلِّمُهُمْ إِذَا خَرَجُوا إِلَى المَقَابِرِ
Kāna-n-nabiyyu ﷺ yuʿallimuhum idhā kharajū ilā-l-maqābir
This greeting was taught, not improvised, and it belongs to the moment of arrival.
يُعَلِّمُهُمْ — root ع ل م. Form II with a continuous kāna: he kept teaching it, which is why the wording is fixed.
السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيَارِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ وَالمُسْلِمِينَ
as-salāmu ʿalaykum ahla-d-diyāri mina-l-muʾminīna wa-l-muslimīn
The dead are addressed as residents and greeted the way living people are greeted.
الدِّيَارِ — root د و ر. Diyār are dwellings, homes people live in. Calling graves that is deliberate.
وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَلَاحِقُونَ
wa-innā in shāʾa-llāhu la-lāḥiqūn
You are not a visitor from a different category. You are next in line.
لَلَاحِقُونَ — root ل ح ق. Lāḥiq is one who catches up. The 'if Allāh wills' attaches to the when, not to the whether.
أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ لَنَا وَلَكُمُ العَافِيَةَ
Asʾalu-llāha lanā wa-lakumu-l-ʿāfiyah
One request covers both sides of the wall: safety for them, safety for us.
العَافِيَةَ — root ع ف و. ʿĀfiyah is being kept sound and clear of harm. For the dead that means safety from what follows.

Chapter 28 — The Supplication for Distress

Book p.70 · المُصِيبَةُ — Affliction · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يَقُولُ عِنْدَ الكَرْبِThe Prophet ﷺ would say at a time of distress
الكِتَابFrom the book

«لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ العَظِيمُ الحَلِيمُ. لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ العَرْشِ العَظِيمِ. لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الأَرْضِ وَرَبُّ العَرْشِ الكَرِيمِ»

✎Added by us

“There is no god but Allāh, the Great, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allāh, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allāh, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne.”

Lā ilāha illa-llāhu-l-ʿaẓīmu-l-ḥalīm. Lā ilāha illa-llāhu rabbu-l-ʿarshi-l-ʿaẓīm. Lā ilāha illa-llāhu rabbu-s-samāwāti wa-rabbu-l-arḍi wa-rabbu-l-ʿarshi-l-karīm.

لَا إِلَهَthere is no god
إِلَّاexcept
اللَّهُAllāh
العَظِيمُthe Great
الحَلِيمُthe Forbearing
لَا إِلَهَthere is no god
إِلَّاexcept
اللَّهُAllāh
رَبُّLord of
العَرْشِthe Throne
العَظِيمِthe Mighty
لَا إِلَهَthere is no god
إِلَّاexcept
اللَّهُAllāh
رَبُّLord of
السَّمَوَاتِthe heavens
وَرَبُّand Lord of
الأَرْضِthe earth
وَرَبُّand Lord of
العَرْشِthe Throne
الكَرِيمِthe Noble
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ العَظِيمُ الحَلِيمُ
Lā ilāha illa-llāhu-l-ʿaẓīmu-l-ḥalīm
In distress the first move is not a request. It is a statement about who Allāh is.
الحَلِيمُ — root ح ل م. Ḥalīm is the one who does not rush to punish. Paired with al-ʿAẓīm: great enough to act, forbearing enough to wait.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ العَرْشِ العَظِيمِ
Lā ilāha illa-llāhu rabbu-l-ʿarshi-l-ʿaẓīm
The same declaration again, now naming His ownership of the greatest created thing.
العَرْشِ — root ع ر ش. The ʿarsh is the highest of creation. Whoever owns it is not troubled by what is troubling you.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الأَرْضِ وَرَبُّ العَرْشِ الكَرِيمِ
Lā ilāha illa-llāhu rabbu-s-samāwāti wa-rabbu-l-arḍi wa-rabbu-l-ʿarshi-l-karīm
A third time, widening: heavens, earth, Throne. Nothing your trouble sits in is outside His.
رَبُّ — root ر ب ب. Rabb is repeated for each realm rather than said once, which slows the words down and settles the one saying them.

قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«وَإِنْ أَصَابَكَ شَيْءٌ، فَلَا تَقُلْ: لَوْ أَنِّي فَعَلْتُ؛ كَانَ كَذَا وَكَذَا. وَلَكِنْ قُلْ: قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ؛ فَإِنَّ لَوْ تَفْتَحُ عَمَلَ الشَّيْطَانِ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay when something you did not want has already happened.
قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ
✎Added by us

“And if something befalls you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such-and-such, then it would have been so-and-so.’ Say instead: ‘It is Allāh's decree, and what He willed He did.’ For ‘if only’ opens up the work of Shayṭān.”

Wa-in aṣābaka shayʾun, fa-lā taqul: law annī faʿaltu; kāna kadhā wa-kadhā. Wa-lākin qul: qadaru-llāhi wa-mā shāʾa faʿal; fa-inna law taftaḥu ʿamala-sh-shayṭān.

وَإِنْand if
أَصَابَكَbefalls you
شَيْءٌsomething
فَلَاthen do not
تَقُلْsay
لَوْif only
أَنِّيI had
فَعَلْتُdone
كَانَit would have been
كَذَاsuch
وَكَذَاand such
وَلَكِنْbut rather
قُلْsay
قَدَرُthe decree of
اللَّهِAllāh
وَمَاand what
شَاءَHe willed
فَعَلَHe did
فَإِنَّfor indeed
لَوْ'if only'
تَفْتَحُopens
عَمَلَthe work of
الشَّيْطَانِShayṭān
وَإِنْ أَصَابَكَ شَيْءٌ، فَلَا تَقُلْ
Wa-in aṣābaka shayʾun, fa-lā taqul
Something lands on you, and the first thing regulated is your speech.
أَصَابَكَ — root ص و ب. Aṣāba is to hit a target. The wording treats the event as aimed, not random.
لَوْ أَنِّي فَعَلْتُ؛ كَانَ كَذَا وَكَذَا
law annī faʿaltu; kāna kadhā wa-kadhā
The banned sentence: replaying a choice that is already closed.
لَوْ — The particle law introduces something contrary to fact. Used about the past it argues with what Allāh has already decided.
وَلَكِنْ قُلْ: قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ
wa-lākin qul: qadaru-llāhi wa-mā shāʾa faʿal
The replacement is short and final. It names the cause and closes the subject.
قَدَرُ — root ق د ر. Qadar is measured determination, not blind fate. Saying it puts the event under Allāh's measure rather than your mistake.
فَإِنَّ لَوْ تَفْتَحُ عَمَلَ الشَّيْطَانِ
fa-inna law taftaḥu ʿamala-sh-shayṭān
The reason for the ban: that kind of regret is a door, and something walks through it.
تَفْتَحُ — root ف ت ح. Taftaḥu is to open. The harm is not the sadness; it is what the sadness gives access to.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

٢
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ تُصِيبُهُ مُصِيبَةٌ، فَيَقُولُ: ﴿إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ﴾. اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي، وَأَخْلِفْ لِي خَيْراً مِنْهَا. إِلَّا أَجَرَهُ اللَّهُ فِي مُصِيبَتِهِ، وَأَخْلَفَ لَهُ خَيْراً مِنْهَا»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay when any loss or affliction reaches you.
﴿إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ﴾. اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي، وَأَخْلِفْ لِي خَيْراً مِنْهَا
✎Added by us

“There is no slave whom a calamity strikes and who then says, ‘Indeed we belong to Allāh, and indeed to Him we are returning. O Allāh, reward me for my calamity, and give me in its place something better than it,’ except that Allāh rewards him for his calamity and gives him in its place something better than it.”

Mā min ʿabdin tuṣībuhu muṣībatun, fa-yaqūl: Innā li-llāhi wa-innā ilayhi rājiʿūn. Allāhumma ʾjurnī fī muṣībatī, wa-akhlif lī khayran minhā. Illā ajarahu-llāhu fī muṣībatihi, wa-akhlafa lahu khayran minhā.

مِنْany
عَبْدٍslave

مُصِيبَةٌa calamity
فَيَقُولُand he says
إِنَّاindeed we
لِلَّهِbelong to Allāh
وَإِنَّاand indeed we
إِلَيْهِto Him
رَاجِعُونَare returning
اللَّهُمَّO Allāh
أْجُرْنِيreward me
فِيin
مُصِيبَتِيmy calamity
وَأَخْلِفْand replace
لِيfor me
خَيْراًsomething better
مِنْهَاthan it
إِلَّاexcept that
أَجَرَهُrewarded him
اللَّهُAllāh
فِيin
مُصِيبَتِهِhis calamity
وَأَخْلَفَand replaced
لَهُfor him
خَيْراًsomething better
مِنْهَاthan it
مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ تُصِيبُهُ مُصِيبَةٌ، فَيَقُولُ
Mā min ʿabdin tuṣībuhu muṣībatun, fa-yaqūl
Any servant, any calamity. The only condition is that he says what follows.
مُصِيبَةٌ — root ص و ب. Muṣībah is anything that strikes, large or small. The promise is not reserved for great losses.
إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ
Innā li-llāhi wa-innā ilayhi rājiʿūn
The Qurʾanic sentence: we are His property, and we are on our way back to Him.
رَاجِعُونَ — root ر ج ع. Rājiʿūn is an active participle, so the returning is in progress now, not only at death.
اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي، وَأَخْلِفْ لِي خَيْراً مِنْهَا
Allāhumma ʾjurnī fī muṣībatī, wa-akhlif lī khayran minhā
Two requests: pay me for this, and put something better where it was.
أْجُرْنِي — root أ ج ر. The book glosses ʾjurnī as: write a reward for me. The book also explains khayran minhā as compensation better than what was lost.
إِلَّا أَجَرَهُ اللَّهُ فِي مُصِيبَتِهِ، وَأَخْلَفَ لَهُ خَيْراً مِنْهَا
Illā ajarahu-llāhu fī muṣībatihi, wa-akhlafa lahu khayran minhā
The answer repeats the request word for word, in the past tense: it is done.
وَأَخْلَفَ — root خ ل ف. Akhlafa is to put a successor in place of something gone. The reply mirrors the duʿāʾ exactly, which is the point of the hadith.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
أْجُرْنِيأَيْ: اكْتُبْ لِي أَجْراً
ajurnī — reward meThat is: record a reward for me.
خَيْراً مِنْهَاأَيْ: عَوِّضْنِي خَيْراً مِمَّا فَاتَنِي فِي هَذِهِ المُصِيبَةِ
khayran minhā — something better than itThat is: compensate me with something better than what I lost in this affliction.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

💎 الفَائِدَة · Deeper lesson
The words begin by remembering the biggest truth — we and everything we love belong to Allah and return to Him — and only then ask for reward and a replacement. Umm Salamah (رضي الله عنها) said it when she lost her husband, thinking none could be better; Allah replaced him with the Prophet ﷺ himself.
✍️ Activityنَشَاط
Memorise the full line so it is ready on your tongue before you need it. Say it for the small setbacks too — a broken plate, a missed chance — not only the large ones.

Chapter 30 — When He Fears a People

Book p.73 · المُصِيبَةُ — Affliction · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا خَافَ قَوْماً قَالَWhen the Prophet ﷺ feared a people he would say
الكِتَابFrom the book

«اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَجْعَلُكَ فِي نُحُورِهِمْ، وَنَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شُرُورِهِمْ»

✎Added by us

“O Allāh, we place You at their throats, and we seek refuge in You from their evils.”

Allāhumma innā najʿaluka fī nuḥūrihim, wa-naʿūdhu bika min shurūrihim.

اللَّهُمَّO Allāh
إِنَّاindeed we
نَجْعَلُكَplace You
فِيat
نُحُورِهِمْtheir throats
وَنَعُوذُand we seek refuge
بِكَin You
مِنْfrom
شُرُورِهِمْtheir evils
اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَجْعَلُكَ فِي نُحُورِهِمْ
Allāhumma innā najʿaluka fī nuḥūrihim
Instead of standing against them yourself, you put Allāh in the space between.
نُحُورِهِمْ — root ن ح ر. The book glosses nuḥūrihim as facing them, directly in front of them. The naḥr is the base of the throat, the nearest point of an advancing enemy.
وَنَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شُرُورِهِمْ
wa-naʿūdhu bika min shurūrihim
Then the plain request: shelter from every kind of harm they carry.
وَنَعُوذُ — root ع و ذ. Naʿūdhu is to take cover with someone stronger. Shurūr is plural, so no single threat is singled out.

نُحُورِهِمْأَيْ: قُبَالَتَهُمْ
nuḥūrihim — their throatsThat is: right in front of them.

Chapter 31 — Supplication Against the Enemy

Book p.74 · المُصِيبَةُ — Affliction · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
دَعَا النَّبِيُّ ﷺ عَلَى الأَحْزَابِ فَقَالَThe Prophet ﷺ supplicated against the confederates and said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«اللَّهُمَّ مُنْزِلَ الكِتَابِ، سَرِيعَ الحِسَابِ، اهْزِمِ الأَحْزَابَ. اللَّهُمَّ اهْزِمْهُمْ وَزَلْزِلْهُمْ»

✎Added by us

“O Allāh, Sender-down of the Book, Swift in reckoning, defeat the confederates. O Allāh, defeat them and shake them.”

Allāhumma munzila-l-kitāb, sarīʿa-l-ḥisāb, ihzimi-l-aḥzāb. Allāhumma-hzimhum wa-zalzilhum.

اللَّهُمَّO Allāh
مُنْزِلَSender-down of
الكِتَابِthe Book
سَرِيعَSwift of
الحِسَابِthe reckoning
اهْزِمِdefeat
الأَحْزَابَthe confederates
اللَّهُمَّO Allāh
اهْزِمْهُمْdefeat them
وَزَلْزِلْهُمْand shake them
اللَّهُمَّ مُنْزِلَ الكِتَابِ، سَرِيعَ الحِسَابِ
Allāhumma munzila-l-kitāb, sarīʿa-l-ḥisāb
Two descriptions come before the request: He revealed the guidance, and He settles accounts fast.
مُنْزِلَ — root ن ز ل. Munzil is the one who sends down. The two titles fit the request: the One who gave the Book is asked about those fighting it.
اهْزِمِ الأَحْزَابَ
ihzimi-l-aḥzāb
One clean request, and the wording plays on the enemy's own name.
الأَحْزَابَ — root ح ز ب. The book identifies al-aḥzāb as the tribes that banded together to fight the Messenger ﷺ at the Battle of the Confederates.
اللَّهُمَّ اهْزِمْهُمْ وَزَلْزِلْهُمْ
Allāhumma-hzimhum wa-zalzilhum
He asks again, adding that their footing itself be shaken.
وَزَلْزِلْهُمْ — root ز ل ز ل. A doubled root for a shaking that repeats. Defeat removes their advance; zalzalah removes their steadiness.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
الأَحْزَابِأَيْ: القَبَائِلِ المُتَجَمِّعَةِ لِحَرْبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي غَزْوَةِ الأَحْزَابِ
al-aḥzāb — the confederatesThat is: the tribes that banded together to fight the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ in the Battle of the Confederates.

مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِAgreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

Chapter 32 — What Is Said to a Traveller in Farewell
الذِّكْرُ — اِحْفَظْ وَاعْمَلْ

Workbook — what the one staying behind says to someone setting out to travel.

About this itemمَتَى وَكَيْف · When & how
When
عِنْدَ تَوْدِيعِ المُسَافِرِ — when seeing a traveller off
Who says it
The resident says it to the one departing
Source
رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيّ · al-Tirmidhī (ṣaḥīḥ)
١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا وَدَّعَ أَحَداً قَالَ لَهُWhen the Prophet ﷺ bade someone farewell he would say to him
الكِتَابFrom the book

«أَسْتَوْدِعُ اللَّهَ دِينَكَ، وَأَمَانَتَكَ، وَخَوَاتِيمَ عَمَلِكَ»

✎Added by us

“I entrust to Allāh your religion, your trust, and the endings of your deeds.”

Astawdiʿu-llāha dīnaka, wa-amānataka, wa-khawātīma ʿamalik.

أَسْتَوْدِعُI entrust to
اللَّهَAllāh
دِينَكَyour religion
وَأَمَانَتَكَand your trust
وَخَوَاتِيمَand the endings of
عَمَلِكَyour deeds
أَسْتَوْدِعُ اللَّهَ
Astawdiʿu-llāha
The whole duʿāʾ is a deposit: you leave something valuable with someone who can keep it.
أَسْتَوْدِعُ — root و د ع. A wadīʿah is property left with another for safekeeping. Form X here means: I make it a deposit with Allāh.
دِينَكَ، وَأَمَانَتَكَ
dīnaka, wa-amānataka
First his religion, then everything left in his care while he travels.
وَأَمَانَتَكَ — root أ م ن. Amānah covers what has been placed in his keeping. The book reads it as his family and the property he left behind.
وَخَوَاتِيمَ عَمَلِكَ
wa-khawātīma ʿamalik
Last, how his deeds end, which is the part no one can arrange for himself.
وَخَوَاتِيمَ — root خ ت م. Khawātīm are seals, final acts. The book explains the whole duʿāʾ: your religion, family, property and your last deeds are all made a deposit with Allāh, that He may seal your affair with good.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
خَوَاتِيمَ عَمَلِكَأَيْ: جَعَلْتُ دِينَكَ، وَأَهْلَكَ، وَمَا تَرَكْتَهُ مِنْ مَالٍ، وَآخِرَ عَمَلِكَ - لِيُخْتَمَ لَكَ بِخَيْرٍ -، جَعَلْتُ كُلَّ ذَلِكَ وَدِيعَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ يَحْفَظُهَا لَكَ
khawātīma ʿamalika — the seals of your deedsThat is: I have placed your religion, your family, the wealth you left behind, and the last of your deeds (so that you may be sealed with good): I have placed all of that in trust with Allāh, who guards it for you.

رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُReported by Aḥmad

💎 الفَائِدَة · Deeper lesson
A farewell that names what truly matters on any journey: not the luggage, but the traveller’s religion, the trusts in their care, and the ending of their deeds. To “entrust to Allah” is to place them in the keeping of the One whose deposits are never lost.
✍️ Activityنَشَاط
Use it as your real goodbye — at the airport, the door, or over the phone: أَسْتَوْدِعُ اللَّهَ دِينَكَ وَأَمَانَتَكَ وَخَوَاتِيمَ عَمَلِكَ.

Chapter 33 — The Supplication for Travel

كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا اسْتَوَى عَلَى بَعِيرِهِ خَارِجاً إِلَى سَفَرٍWhen the Prophet ﷺ had mounted his camel setting out on a journey
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كَبَّرَ - ثَلَاثاً -، ثُمَّ قَالَ: ﴿سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ ۞ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا البِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ العَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى. اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا، وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ. اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالخَلِيفَةُ فِي الأَهْلِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ المَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ المُنْقَلَبِ فِي المَالِ وَالأَهْلِ. وَإِذَا رَجَعَ قَالَهُنَّ، وَزَادَ فِيهِنَّ: آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ»

ثَلَاثاًthree times

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay once you are settled on your transport at the start of a journey. On the way home say the same and add the four words at the end of this entry: آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ (āyibūn, tāʾibūn, ʿābidūn, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn).
﴿سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ ۞ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا البِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ العَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى. اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا، وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ. اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالخَلِيفَةُ فِي الأَهْلِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ المَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ المُنْقَلَبِ فِي المَالِ وَالأَهْلِ
✎Added by us

He said the takbīr three times, then said: “Glory be to Him who has put this at our service, when we ourselves were not equal to it, and indeed to our Lord we are returning. O Allāh, we ask You on this journey of ours for righteousness and godfearing, and for deeds that please You. O Allāh, make this journey of ours light for us, and fold up its distance for us. O Allāh, You are the Companion on the journey and the Guardian over the family. O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from a grim sight, and from an evil homecoming in property and family.” And when he returned he said them again, and added to them: “Returning, repenting, worshipping, giving praise to our Lord.”

Kabbara - thalāthan -, thumma qāl: Subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa-mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn, wa-innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn. Allāhumma innā nasʾaluka fī safarinā hādhā-l-birra wa-t-taqwā, wa-mina-l-ʿamali mā tarḍā. Allāhumma hawwin ʿalaynā safaranā hādhā, wa-ṭwi ʿannā buʿdah. Allāhumma anta-ṣ-ṣāḥibu fī-s-safar, wa-l-khalīfatu fī-l-ahl. Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika min waʿthāʾi-s-safar, wa-kaʾābati-l-manẓar, wa-sūʾi-l-munqalabi fī-l-māli wa-l-ahl. Wa-idhā rajaʿa qālahunna, wa-zāda fīhinna: āyibūn, tāʾibūn, ʿābidūn, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn.

كَبَّرَ - ثَلَاثاً -، ثُمَّ قَالَ: ﴿سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ ۞ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ
Kabbara - thalāthan -, thumma qāl: Subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa-mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn, wa-innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn
Three takbīrs, then the āyah of travel: this mount was given to us, and the road ends at our Lord.
مُقْرِنِينَ — root ق ر ن. The book glosses muqrinīn as capable, able to manage it. The rider admits the animal, or the engine, was never his to master.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا البِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ العَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى
Allāhumma innā nasʾaluka fī safarinā hādhā-l-birra wa-t-taqwā, wa-mina-l-ʿamali mā tarḍā
The first request is not comfort. It is that the journey be spent well.
البِرَّ — root ب ر ر. Birr is doing good broadly; taqwā is guarding against wrong. Asked together, they cover both halves of conduct on the road.
اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا، وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ
Allāhumma hawwin ʿalaynā safaranā hādhā, wa-ṭwi ʿannā buʿdah
Now the road itself: lighten it, and shorten what is long about it.
وَاطْوِ — root ط و ي. Ṭawā is to fold cloth. The book reads it: bring the distance of this journey near for us. Hawwin, the book says, means lighten its hardships.
اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالخَلِيفَةُ فِي الأَهْلِ
Allāhumma anta-ṣ-ṣāḥibu fī-s-safar, wa-l-khalīfatu fī-l-ahl
Two places at once, and Allāh is asked for both: beside the traveller, and over what he left.
وَالخَلِيفَةُ — root خ ل ف. The book explains: You guard my family in my absence. Ṣāḥib, it says, is the one who stays with us on the road with care and protection.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ المَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ المُنْقَلَبِ فِي المَالِ وَالأَهْلِ
Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika min waʿthāʾi-s-safar, wa-kaʾābati-l-manẓar, wa-sūʾi-l-munqalabi fī-l-māli wa-l-ahl
Three fears named plainly: the strain of the road, grim sights, and coming home to bad news.
وَعْثَاءِ — root و ع ث. The book glosses waʿthāʾ as its hardship. Kaʾābah, it says, is ugliness of what you see; al-munqalab is the return.
وَإِذَا رَجَعَ قَالَهُنَّ، وَزَادَ فِيهِنَّ: آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ
Wa-idhā rajaʿa qālahunna, wa-zāda fīhinna: āyibūn, tāʾibūn, ʿābidūn, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn
The homeward version is the same words plus four: back, repentant, still worshipping, still praising.
آيِبُونَ — root أ و ب. The book glosses āyibūn as returning. Arriving home is treated as a reason to repent and praise, not only to rest.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
مُقْرِنِينَأَيْ: مُطِيقِينَ
muqrinīn — able to master itThat is: capable of it.
لَمُنْقَلِبُونَأَيْ: صَائِرُونَ إِلَيْهِ بَعْدَ مَمَاتِنَا
la-munqalibūn — surely returningThat is: bound for Him after our death.
هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَاأَيْ: خَفِّفْ عَلَيْنَا مَشَاقَّهُ
hawwin ʿalaynā safaranā hādhā — ease this journey for usThat is: lighten its hardships for us.
وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُأَيْ: قَرِّبْ لَنَا بُعْدَ هَذَا السَّفَرِ
wa-ṭwi ʿannā buʿdahu — fold up its distance for usThat is: bring near for us the far distance of this journey.
الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِأَيْ: المُلَازِمُ لَنَا فِي السَّفَرِ بِالعِنَايَةِ وَالحِفْظِ
al-ṣāḥib fī al-safar — the Companion on the journeyThat is: the One who stays close to us on the journey with care and protection.
وَالخَلِيفَةُ فِي الأَهْلِأَيْ: تَحْفَظُ أَهْلِي فِي غَيْبَتِي
wa-l-khalīfah fī al-ahl — the Guardian over the familyThat is: You protect my family in my absence.
وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِأَيْ: مَشَقَّتِهِ
waʿthāʾ al-safar — the rigours of travelThat is: its hardship.
كَآبَةِ المَنْظَرِأَيْ: قُبْحِهِ
kaʾābat al-manẓar — a grim sightThat is: its ugliness.
المُنْقَلَبِأَيْ: الرُّجُوعِ
al-munqalab — the returnThat is: the going back.
آيِبُونَأَيْ: رَاجِعُونَ
āʾibūn — we are returningThat is: coming back.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

💎 الفَائِدَة · Deeper lesson
Before asking for anything, the traveller declares Allah greatest and remembers that the very vehicle beneath them was subjected by Allah — they could never have tamed it alone. Only then come the requests: not a safe trip first, but righteousness, piety, and pleasing deeds — then ease and a shortened distance.
⭐ Companion and Guardian
The ending is a comfort for both sides of the journey: anta-ṣ-ṣāḥibu fi-s-safar — Allah travels with you — wa-l-khalīfatu fi-l-ahl — and stays behind as Guardian over the family you left.
✍️ Activityنَشَاط
Say it at the start of every trip this month — a flight, a drive, even a long commute — once you are seated and about to set off.

What does the traveller do before making any request?

Chapter 34 — When He Ascends or Descends on His Journey

Book p.80 · السَّفَرُ — Travel · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ جَابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَاJābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh (may Allāh be pleased with them both) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كُنَّا إِذَا صَعِدْنَا كَبَّرْنَا. وَإِذَا نَزَلْنَا سَبَّحْنَا»

✎Added by us

“Whenever we climbed, we said the takbīr. And whenever we went down, we said the tasbīḥ.”

Kunnā idhā ṣaʿidnā kabbarnā. Wa-idhā nazalnā sabbaḥnā.

Going up, they answered the height by declaring Allāh greater: Allāhu akbar.
كَبَّرْنَا — root ك ب ر. The book glosses ṣaʿidnā as rising to high ground. Height in front of you is met by naming the One who is above it.

Going down, they said Subḥāna-llāh, declaring Him far above any lowness.
سَبَّحْنَا — root س ب ح. Tasbīḥ is removing every defect from Allāh. The book glosses nazalnā as going down to low ground, so the words fit the descent.

Chapter 35 — When the Traveller Reaches the Last Hours of the Night

Book p.81 · السَّفَرُ — Travel · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا كَانَ فِي سَفَرٍ وَأَسْحَرَ يَقُولُWhen the Prophet ﷺ was on a journey and the last part of the night came, he would say
الكِتَابFrom the book

«سَمِعَ سَامِعٌ بِحَمْدِ اللَّهِ، وَحُسْنِ بَلَائِهِ عَلَيْنَا. رَبَّنَا صَاحِبْنَا، وَأَفْضِلْ عَلَيْنَا. عَائِذاً بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ»

✎Added by us

“Let a hearer hear our praise of Allāh and of the goodness of His favour upon us. Our Lord, be our companion and be generous to us. Seeking refuge in Allāh from the Fire.”

Samiʿa sāmiʿun bi-ḥamdi-llāh, wa-ḥusni balāʾihi ʿalaynā. Rabbanā ṣāḥibnā, wa-afḍil ʿalaynā. ʿĀʾidhan bi-llāhi mina-n-nār.

Samiʿa sāmiʿun bi-ḥamdi-llāh, wa-ḥusni balāʾihi ʿalaynā
Said aloud in the last dark of the night: let whoever is awake hear us thanking Allāh.
بَلَائِهِ — root ب ل و. Balāʾ can mean trial or favour; here the book reads it as favour. Its gloss: let the hearer hear our praise of Allāh and our acknowledgement of the goodness of His blessing.
رَبَّنَا صَاحِبْنَا، وَأَفْضِلْ عَلَيْنَا
Rabbanā ṣāḥibnā, wa-afḍil ʿalaynā
Two requests for the road ahead: company, and more than you deserve.
صَاحِبْنَا — root ص ح ب. The book explains it: be a companion to us on our journey and guard us in it. Afḍil, it says, means bestow favour on us.
عَائِذاً بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ
ʿĀʾidhan bi-llāhi mina-n-nār
The night ends with the one thing worth fleeing, and it is not the road's danger.
عَائِذاً — root ع و ذ. ʿĀʾidhan is a participle in the accusative, describing the speaker's own state: I say this as one taking refuge.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
أَسْحَرَأَيْ: دَخَلَ فِي وَقْتِ السَّحَرِ؛ وَهُوَ مَا قَبْلَ الفَجْرِ
asḥara — he reached the pre-dawnThat is: he entered the time of saḥar, which is the part of the night before dawn.
وَحُسْنِ بَلَائِهِ عَلَيْنَاأَيْ: لِيَسْمَعِ السَّامِعُ حَمْدَنَا لِلَّهِ، وَاعْتِرَافَنَا بِحُسْنِ إِنْعَامِهِ
wa-ḥusni balāʾihi ʿalaynā — His excellent favour upon usThat is: so the hearer may hear our praise of Allāh and our acknowledgement of the goodness of His bounty.
صَاحِبْنَاأَيْ: كُنْ صَاحِباً لَنَا فِي سَفَرِنَا تَحْفَظُنَا فِيهِ
ṣāḥibnā — accompany usThat is: be a companion to us on our journey, protecting us on it.
وَأَفْضِلْ عَلَيْنَاأَيْ: أَنْعِمْ عَلَيْنَا
wa-afḍil ʿalaynā — and bestow favour on usThat is: grant us Your bounty.

Chapter 36 — Entering a Town

Book p.82 · السَّفَرُ — Travel · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
لَمْ يَرَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ قَرْيَةً يُرِيدُ دُخُولَهَا؛ إِلَّا قَالَ حِينَ يَرَاهَاThe Prophet ﷺ never saw a town he intended to enter without saying, when he saw it
الكِتَابFrom the book

«اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمَوَاتِ السَّبْعِ وَمَا أَظْلَلْنَ. وَرَبَّ الأَرَضِينَ وَمَا أَقْلَلْنَ. وَرَبَّ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَمَا أَضْلَلْنَ. وَرَبَّ الرِّيَاحِ وَمَا ذَرَيْنَ. فَإِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ هَذِهِ القَرْيَةِ، وَخَيْرَ أَهْلِهَا. وَنَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا، وَشَرِّ أَهْلِهَا، وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهَا»

✎Added by us

“O Allāh, Lord of the seven heavens and all they shade, Lord of the earths and all they carry, Lord of the devils and all they lead astray, Lord of the winds and all they scatter: we ask You for the good of this town and the good of its people, and we seek refuge in You from its evil, from the evil of its people, and from the evil of what is in it.”

Allāhumma rabba-s-samāwāti-s-sabʿi wa-mā aẓlaln. Wa-rabba-l-araḍīna wa-mā aqlaln. Wa-rabba-sh-shayāṭīni wa-mā aḍlaln. Wa-rabba-r-riyāḥi wa-mā dharayn. Fa-innā nasʾaluka khayra hādhihi-l-qaryati, wa-khayra ahlihā. Wa-naʿūdhu bika min sharrihā, wa-sharri ahlihā, wa-sharri mā fīhā.

اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمَوَاتِ السَّبْعِ وَمَا أَظْلَلْنَ
Allāhumma rabba-s-samāwāti-s-sabʿi wa-mā aẓlaln
Before asking anything, the duʿāʾ names who owns the sky and everything under its shade.
أَظْلَلْنَ — root ظ ل ل. The book glosses aẓlaln as what they covered beneath them. The verb is feminine plural, agreeing with the seven heavens.
وَرَبَّ الأَرَضِينَ وَمَا أَقْلَلْنَ
wa-rabba-l-araḍīna wa-mā aqlaln
Then the earths and their whole load, which includes the town you are looking at.
أَقْلَلْنَ — root ق ل ل. The book glosses aqlaln as what they carried. Aqalla is to lift and bear a weight.
وَرَبَّ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَمَا أَضْلَلْنَ. وَرَبَّ الرِّيَاحِ وَمَا ذَرَيْنَ
wa-rabba-sh-shayāṭīni wa-mā aḍlaln, wa-rabba-r-riyāḥi wa-mā dharayn
Even the devils and what they misguide are under His lordship, and so are the winds.
أَضْلَلْنَ — root ض ل ل. The book notes aḍlaln is from ḍalālah, the opposite of guidance. Dharayn, it says, means what they moved along.
فَإِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ هَذِهِ القَرْيَةِ، وَخَيْرَ أَهْلِهَا
fa-innā nasʾaluka khayra hādhihi-l-qaryati, wa-khayra ahlihā
Now the request: the good of the place, and the good of the people in it.
خَيْرَ — root خ ي ر. Khayr is asked for the town and its people separately, because a place can be good while its people are not.
وَنَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا، وَشَرِّ أَهْلِهَا، وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهَا
wa-naʿūdhu bika min sharrihā, wa-sharri ahlihā, wa-sharri mā fīhā
The same three, in the negative, with a catch-all at the end for whatever you have not thought of.
شَرِّهَا — root ش ر ر. Sharr is repeated three times, once for the place, once for the people, once for anything else. The last phrase is deliberately open.

أَضْلَلْنَمِنَ الضَّلَالَةِ؛ ضِدِّ الهِدَايَةِ

ذَرَيْنَأَيْ: وَمَا نَقَلْنَ

Chapter 37 — Returning from a Journey

Book p.84 · السَّفَرُ — Travel · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا قَفَلَ مِنْ غَزْوٍ، أَوْ حَجٍّ، أَوْ عُمْرَةٍ: يُكَبِّرُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَرَفٍ مِنَ الأَرْضِ - ثَلَاثَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ -، ثُمَّ يَقُولُWhen the Prophet ﷺ returned from a military expedition, or a Ḥajj, or an ʿUmrah, he would say the takbīr on every elevation of the ground - three takbīrs - then say
الكِتَابFrom the book

«لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ. آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، سَاجِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ. صَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ»

ثَلَاثَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍthree takbīrs

✎Added by us

The Prophet ﷺ, when he came back from a campaign, or from Hajj, or from ʿUmrah, would say the takbīr on every rise in the ground (three takbīrs), then say: “There is no god but Allāh, alone, with no partner. His is the dominion, and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things. We are returning, repenting, worshipping, prostrating, and praising our Lord. Allāh has kept His promise true, and given victory to His servant, and routed the massed armies alone.”

Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lahu, lahu-l-mulku, wa-lahu-l-ḥamdu, wa-huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr. Āyibūna, tāʾibūna, ʿābidūna, sājidūna, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn. Ṣadaqa-llāhu waʿdahu, wa-naṣara ʿabdahu, wa-hazama-l-aḥzāba waḥdah

Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah
The journey home opens where everything opens: no god but Allāh, and no partner beside Him.
وَحْدَهُ — root و ح د. Waḥdahu means He alone did it. Said on arriving safely, it hands the whole trip back to Allāh.
لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
lahu-l-mulku, wa-lahu-l-ḥamdu, wa-huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr
Ownership is His and praise is His, and nothing at all sits outside His power.
قَدِيرٌ — root ق د ر. Qadīr is the intensive form: fully able, and the reach given is 'every thing'.
آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، سَاجِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ
Āyibūna, tāʾibūna, ʿābidūna, sājidūna, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn
Five words for the people coming back: returning, repenting, worshipping, prostrating, praising.
آيِبُونَ — root أ و ب. Āyib is one who returns. The same root gives awwāb, the person who keeps turning back to Allāh.
صَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ
Ṣadaqa-llāhu waʿdahu, wa-naṣara ʿabdahu, wa-hazama-l-aḥzāba waḥdah
Three things are stated as done: the promise kept, the servant helped, the armies broken.
الأَحْزَابَ — root ح ز ب. Al-Aḥzāb were the confederate tribes that massed against Madīnah and left without a battle.

قَفَلَأَيْ: رَجَعَ

شَرَفٍأَيْ: مَوْضِعٍ عَالٍ
sharaf — high groundThat is: an elevated place.

Chapter 38 — The Talbiyah

Book p.88 · الحَجُّ — The Ḥajj · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
كَانَتْ تَلْبِيَةُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺThe talbiyah of the Prophet ﷺ was
الكِتَابFrom the book

«لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ. لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ. إِنَّ الحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ»

✎Added by us

The talbiyah of the Prophet ﷺ was: “Here I am, O Allāh, here I am. Here I am; You have no partner; here I am. The praise and the favour are Yours, and the dominion. You have no partner.”

Labbayka-llāhumma labbayk. Labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. Inna-l-ḥamda wa-n-niʿmata laka wa-l-mulk, lā sharīka lak

The pilgrim is answering a call, not starting a conversation: I have come, I am here.
لَبَّيْكَ — root ل ب ب. The book glosses it: I have answered You, my Lord, to what You called me to, answer after answer. The doubled form is the repeating.
لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ
labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk
Between two answers he states what he is answering: One with no partner.
شَرِيكَ — root ش ر ك. A sharīk is a partner holding a share. The talbiyah refuses to give anyone a share.
إِنَّ الحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالمُلْكَ
inna-l-ḥamda wa-n-niʿmata laka wa-l-mulk
Praise, every favour received, and the kingdom are all put on one side: His.
وَالنِّعْمَةَ — root ن ع م. Niʿmah is a favour given to you. Naming it here credits the journey itself to Allāh.
لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
lā sharīka lak
It closes on the same line it stood on: no partner.

Chapter 39 — The Black Stone

Book p.89 · الحَجُّ — The Ḥajj · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
الحَجَرُ الأَسْوَدُḤadīth

«طَافَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ بِالبَيْتِ وَهُوَ عَلَى بَعِيرٍ؛ كُلَّمَا أَتَى عَلَى الرُّكْنِ أَشَارَ إِلَيْهِ بِشَيْءٍ فِي يَدِهِ، وَكَبَّرَ»

Chapter 40 — The Duʿāʾ Between the Two Corners

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يَقُولُ مَا بَيْنَ الرُّكْنَيْنِThe Prophet ﷺ would say between the two corners
الكِتَابFrom the book

«﴿رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِى ٱلْأَخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾»

✎Added by us

The Prophet ﷺ used to say, in the stretch between the two Corners: “Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and shield us from the punishment of the Fire.”

Rabbanā ātinā fi-d-dunyā ḥasanatan wa-fi-l-ākhirati ḥasanatan wa-qinā ʿadhāba-n-nār

Said between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone: ask for good in this life first.
حَسَنَةً — root ح س ن. Ḥasanah is left indefinite: any good thing. Health, lawful earning and a sound family all fall inside it.
وَفِى ٱلْأَخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً
wa-fi-l-ākhirati ḥasanah
Then the same request, word for word, for the life after this one.
ٱلْأَخِرَةِ — root أ خ ر. Al-Ākhirah is 'the last one'. The two lives are asked for in one breath, not set against each other.
وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
wa-qinā ʿadhāba-n-nār
One thing is asked to be kept away: the punishment of the Fire.
وَقِنَا — root و ق ي. To shield. Taqwā is from the same root: putting something between yourself and harm.
