Allāhumma innī asʾaluka-l-ʿāfiyata fī-d-dunyā wa-l-ākhirah
The first request is broad: soundness in both lives.
العَافِيَةَ — root ع ف و. ʿĀfiyah is being kept whole and unharmed, in body, religion and circumstance.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ العَفْوَ وَالعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي.
Allāhumma innī asʾaluka-l-ʿafwa wa-l-ʿāfiyata fī dīnī wa-dunyāya wa-ahlī wa-mālī
The same request itemised across the four things a person can lose.
العَفْوَ — root ع ف و. Same root as ʿāfiyah. ʿAfw is having sins passed over; ʿāfiyah is being spared harm. Both are asked at once.
اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي، وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي.
Allāhumma-stur ʿawrātī, wa-āmin rawʿātī
Two requests for the inner life: keep my faults covered, settle my alarms.
رَوْعَاتِي — root ر و ع. The book glosses ar-rawʿ as fright. Rawʿāt are the moments of panic, and safety is asked in them.
اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْنِي مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ، وَمِنْ خَلْفِي، وَعَنْ يَمِينِي، وَعَنْ شِمَالِي، وَمِنْ فَوْقِي.
Allāhumma-ḥfaẓnī min bayni yadayya, wa-min khalfī, wa-ʿan yamīnī, wa-ʿan shimālī, wa-min fawqī
Five directions are named one by one, so nothing is left open.
احْفَظْنِي — root ح ف ظ. Ḥifẓ is keeping something under guard. The list is exhaustive on purpose.
وَأَعُوذُ بِعَظَمَتِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِي
Wa-aʿūdhu bi-ʿaẓamatika an ughtāla min taḥtī
The sixth direction is handled differently: refuge is taken in Allāh's greatness.
أُغْتَالَ — root غ و ل. A passive Form VIII, to be taken suddenly. The book glosses it: destroyed by the earth caving in.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
رَوْعَاتِيالرَّوْعُ: الفَزَعُ
rawʿātī — my terrorsal-rawʿ: fright.
أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِيأَيْ: أُهْلَكَ بِالخَسْفِ
ughtāla min taḥtī — that I be seized from beneath meThat is: that I be destroyed by the earth caving in.

رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُReported by Aḥmad

١٠
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«سَيِّدُ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ أَنْ تَقُولَ: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ. وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ. أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ. أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ. وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي؛ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ. قَالَ: وَمَنْ قَالَهَا مِنَ النَّهَارِ مُوقِناً بِهَا، فَمَاتَ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُمْسِيَ؛ فَهُوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الجَنَّةِ. وَمَنْ قَالَهَا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَهُوَ مُوقِنٌ بِهَا، فَمَاتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصْبِحَ؛ فَهُوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الجَنَّةِ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay morning and evening, meaning every word of it.
اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ. وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ. أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ. أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ. وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي؛ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
✎Added by us

“The master of asking forgiveness is that you say: O Allāh, You are my Lord, there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant. I hold to Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge with You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge before You Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge before You my sin, so forgive me; for none forgives sins but You.” He said: “Whoever says it during the day, certain of it, and dies that day of his before evening comes, he is among the people of Paradise. And whoever says it during the night, certain of it, and dies before morning comes, he is among the people of Paradise.”

Sayyidu-l-istighfāri an taqūl: Allāhumma anta rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa-anā ʿabduk. Wa-anā ʿalā ʿahdika wa-waʿdika mā-staṭaʿt. Aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt. Abūʾu laka bi-niʿmatika ʿalayy. Wa-abūʾu laka bi-dhanbī, fa-ghfir lī; fa-innahu lā yaghfiru-dh-dhunūba illā ant. Qāla: Wa-man qālahā mina-n-nahāri mūqinan bihā, fa-māta min yawmihi qabla an yumsī; fa-huwa min ahli-l-jannah. Wa-man qālahā mina-l-layli wa-huwa mūqinun bihā, fa-māta qabla an yuṣbiḥ; fa-huwa min ahli-l-jannah

الجَنَّةِParadise
سَيِّدُ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ أَنْ تَقُولَ:
Sayyidu-l-istighfāri an taqūl
One wording is singled out above every other way of asking forgiveness.
سَيِّدُ — root س و د. The book notes there are several forms of istighfār; this one is called their master.
اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ.
Allāhumma anta rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa-anā ʿabduk
It opens by settling who is who: You are Lord, I am the created servant.
عَبْدُكَ — root ع ب د. Being created is stated first, so servanthood follows as a fact rather than a claim.
وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ.
Wa-anā ʿalā ʿahdika wa-waʿdika mā-staṭaʿt
A commitment is made, with an honest limit attached to it.
اسْتَطَعْتُ — root ط و ع. Mā istaṭaʿt, as far as I am able. The pledge is real but not overstated.
أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ.
Aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt
Refuge from the harm of his own actions comes before the request itself.
صَنَعْتُ — root ص ن ع. Ṣanaʿa is to make or work something. The evil asked against is his own manufacture.
أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ. وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي؛ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ.
Abūʾu laka bi-niʿmatika ʿalayy. Wa-abūʾu laka bi-dhanbī, fa-ghfir lī; fa-innahu lā yaghfiru-dh-dhunūba illā ant
Two admissions in the same words, His favour and my sin, and then the request.
أَبُوءُ — root ب و أ. The book glosses it: I confess. Using it for the favour and for the sin alike is the point.
قَالَ: وَمَنْ قَالَهَا مِنَ النَّهَارِ مُوقِناً بِهَا، فَمَاتَ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُمْسِيَ؛ فَهُوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الجَنَّةِ. وَمَنْ قَالَهَا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَهُوَ مُوقِنٌ بِهَا، فَمَاتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصْبِحَ؛ فَهُوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الجَنَّةِ
Qāla: Wa-man qālahā mina-n-nahāri mūqinan bihā, fa-māta min yawmihi qabla an yumsī; fa-huwa min ahli-l-jannah. Wa-man qālahā mina-l-layli wa-huwa mūqinun bihā, fa-māta qabla an yuṣbiḥ; fa-huwa min ahli-l-jannah
The reward: dying after saying it in conviction, by day or by night, means Paradise.
مُوقِناً — root ي ق ن. Yaqīn is certainty with no doubt left in it. The condition is not the saying on its own.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
سَيِّدُ الِاسْتِغْفَارِلِلِاسْتِغْفَارِ عِدَّةُ صِيَغٍ؛ مِنْهَا: «أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ»، «رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي»، «غُفْرَانَكَ»، وَأَفْضَلُ صِيَغِ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ: مَا وَرَدَ فِي هَذَا الحَدِيثِ
sayyid al-istighfār — the foremost formula of seeking forgivenessSeeking forgiveness has several formulas, among them: “I seek Allāh's forgiveness”, “My Lord, forgive me”, “Your forgiveness”. And the best of the formulas of seeking forgiveness is what comes in this hadith.
أَبُوءُأَيْ: أَعْتَرِفُ
abūʾu — I acknowledgeThat is: I confess.

رَوَاهُ البُخَارِيُّReported by al-Bukhārī

١١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ قَالَ - حِينَ يُصْبِحُ وَحِينَ يُمْسِي -: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ؛ لَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ بِأَفْضَلَ مِمَّا جَاءَ بِهِ؛ إِلَّا أَحَدٌ قَالَ مِثْلَ مَا قَالَ، أَوْ زَادَ عَلَيْهِ»

مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍa hundred times

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay a hundred times morning and evening.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
✎Added by us

“Whoever says, when he enters the morning and when he enters the evening: Glory be to Allāh and praise be to Him, a hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than what he came with, except someone who said the like of what he said, or added to it.”

Man qāla (ḥīna yuṣbiḥu wa-ḥīna yumsī): Subḥāna-llāhi wa-bi-ḥamdih, miʾata marrah; lam yaʾti aḥadun yawma-l-qiyāmati bi-afḍala mimmā jāʾa bih; illā aḥadun qāla mithla mā qāl, aw zāda ʿalayh

مَنْwhoever

يُصْبِحُhe enters the morning
وَحِينَand when
يُمْسِيhe enters the evening
سُبْحَانَglory be to
اللَّهِAllāh
وَبِحَمْدِهِand praise be to Him
مِئَةَa hundred
مَرَّةٍtimes
لَمْwill not
يَأْتِcome
أَحَدٌanyone
يَوْمَon the Day of
القِيَامَةِResurrection
بِأَفْضَلَwith better
مِمَّاthan what
جَاءَhe came
بِهِwith
إِلَّاexcept
أَحَدٌsomeone
قَالَwho said
مِثْلَthe like of
مَاwhat
قَالَhe said
أَوْor
زَادَadded
عَلَيْهِto it
مَنْ قَالَ - حِينَ يُصْبِحُ وَحِينَ يُمْسِي -:
Man qāla (ḥīna yuṣbiḥu wa-ḥīna yumsī)
The time is set as in the rest of this chapter: both ends of the day.
حِينَ — root ح ي ن. Ḥīna yuṣbiḥ is the moment of becoming morning, not the whole morning.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ؛
Subḥāna-llāhi wa-bi-ḥamdih, miʾata marrah
Four words, said a hundred times, joining glorification to praise.
سُبْحَانَ — root س ب ح. Tasbīḥ clears Allāh of any flaw; ḥamd affirms what is due to Him. The pair covers both sides.
لَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ بِأَفْضَلَ مِمَّا جَاءَ بِهِ؛
lam yaʾti aḥadun yawma-l-qiyāmati bi-afḍala mimmā jāʾa bih
The measure is taken on the Day of Resurrection, against what everyone else brings.
بِأَفْضَلَ — root ف ض ل. Afḍal is a comparative: better than. The comparison is with other people's record, not a fixed total.
إِلَّا أَحَدٌ قَالَ مِثْلَ مَا قَالَ، أَوْ زَادَ عَلَيْهِ
illā aḥadun qāla mithla mā qāl, aw zāda ʿalayh
One exception is allowed, and it is open to anybody: say the same, or say more.
زَادَ — root ز ي د. The door is left open. Nobody is shut out of the same standing.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

١٢
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ - مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ إِذَا أَصْبَحَ، وَمِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ إِذَا أَمْسَى -؛ لَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ بِأَفْضَلَ مِنْهُ؛ إِلَّا مَنْ قَالَ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ»

مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ إِذَا أَصْبَحَ، وَمِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ إِذَا أَمْسَىa hundred times in the morning, and a hundred times in the evening

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay a hundred times in the morning and a hundred in the evening.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
✎Added by us

“Whoever says: There is no god but Allāh, alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things, a hundred times when he enters the morning and a hundred times when he enters the evening, no one will come with anything better than his, except one who said something better than that.”

Man qāla: Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahu-l-mulku, wa-lahu-l-ḥamdu, wa-huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr (miʾata marratin idhā aṣbaḥa, wa-miʾata marratin idhā amsā); lam yaʾti aḥadun bi-afḍala minh; illā man qāla afḍala min dhālik

مَنْ قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ،
Man qāla: Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah
The dhikr opens with the testimony, then rules out any partner immediately.
وَحْدَهُ — root و ح د. Waḥdahu, Him alone, and lā sharīka lah says the same thing again as a denial.
لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
lahu-l-mulku, wa-lahu-l-ḥamdu, wa-huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr
Three things are affirmed of Him: the kingdom, the praise, and power over all.
قَدِيرٌ — root ق د ر. Qadīr is one whose power actually takes effect. ʿAlā kulli shayʾ allows no exception.
- مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ إِذَا أَصْبَحَ، وَمِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ إِذَا أَمْسَى -؛
(miʾata marratin idhā aṣbaḥa, wa-miʾata marratin idhā amsā)
A hundred in the morning and a hundred in the evening, counted separately.
مِئَةَ — root م أ ي. The count is deliberate: two hundred a day, split between the two ends of it.
لَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ بِأَفْضَلَ مِنْهُ؛ إِلَّا مَنْ قَالَ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
lam yaʾti aḥadun bi-afḍala minh; illā man qāla afḍala min dhālik
Nobody outdoes him on that Day, unless they bring something greater still.
بِأَفْضَلَ — root ف ض ل. The same comparative as the hadith before it, and the same open exception.

تَعْوِيذُ الأَوْلَادِ

Chapter 59 — Seeking Refuge for Children

Book p.139 · أَذْكَارُ الصَّبَاحِ وَالمَسَاءِ — Morning & Evening · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يُعَوِّذُ الحَسَنَ وَالحُسَيْنَ، وَيَقُولُThe Prophet ﷺ would seek protection for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, saying
الكِتَابFrom the book

«إِنَّ أَبَاكُمَا كَانَ يُعَوِّذُ بِهَا إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay it over a child. The book notes he need not be near you, and it may be said for a wife, a mother, or anyone else.
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
✎Added by us

The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, saying: “Your father used to seek refuge with these words for Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allāh from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every eye that harms.”

Inna abākumā kāna yuʿawwidhu bihā Ismāʿīla wa-Isḥāq: Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmah, min kulli shayṭānin wa-hāmmah, wa-min kulli ʿaynin lāmmah

إِنَّ أَبَاكُمَا كَانَ يُعَوِّذُ بِهَا إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ:
Inna abākumā kāna yuʿawwidhu bihā Ismāʿīla wa-Isḥāq
The Prophet ﷺ tells the two boys that Ibrāhīm said this over his own two sons.
أَبَاكُمَا — root أ ب و. The book glosses it: Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. The practice is being handed down, not invented.
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ،
Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmah
Refuge is taken in the words of Allāh, described as complete.
التَّامَّةِ — root ت م م. Tāmmah, complete: nothing is missing in them, so nothing gets through them.
مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ،
min kulli shayṭānin wa-hāmmah
Two dangers together: devils, and anything that carries venom.
وَهَامَّةٍ — root ه م م. The book glosses al-hāmmah: every creature that has venom in it.
وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
wa-min kulli ʿaynin lāmmah
And the eye: the envious look that brings harm with it.
لَامَّةٍ — root ل م م. The book glosses al-lāmmah: the eye that strikes a person with harm.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
يُعَوِّذُ الحَسَنَ وَالحُسَيْنَلَا يُشْتَرَطُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الوَلَدُ قَرِيباً مِنْكَ، فَلَكَ أَنْ تَقُولَ هَذَا الدُّعَاءَ وَإِنْ كَانَ بَعِيداً عَنْكَ، وَيَصِحُّ تَعْوِيذُ غَيْرِ الوَلَدِ؛ كَالزَّوْجَةِ وَالأُمِّ وَغَيْرِهِمَا
yuʿawwidhu al-Ḥasan wa-l-Ḥusayn — he sought protection for al-Ḥasan and al-ḤusaynIt is not a condition that the child be near you, so you may say this supplication even if he is far from you. And seeking protection for someone other than a child is valid, such as a wife, a mother, and others.

abākumā — your fatherThat is: Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him).

التَّسْبِيحُ وَالتَّحْمِيدُ

Chapter 60 — Glorifying and Praising Allāh

Book p.142 · أَذْكَارٌ عَامَّةٌ — General Adhkār · 6 entries in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ قَالَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ العَظِيمِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ؛ غُرِسَتْ لَهُ نَخْلَةٌ فِي الجَنَّةِ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay at any time; each saying plants a palm.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ العَظِيمِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
✎Added by us

“Whoever says, ‘Glory be to Allāh the Great, and praise be to Him,’ a date palm is planted for him in Paradise.”

Man qāla: Subḥāna-llāhi-l-ʿAẓīmi wa bi-ḥamdih; ghurisat lahu nakhlatun fī-l-jannah

مَنْwhoever
قَالَsays
سُبْحَانَglory be to
اللَّهِAllāh
العَظِيمِthe Great
وَبِحَمْدِهِand praise be to Him
غُرِسَتْwas planted
لَهُfor him

فِيin
الجَنَّةِParadise
مَنْ قَالَ
Man qāla
The offer is open to anyone at all who says the words.
قَالَ — root ق و ل. Qāla is plain speech. Nothing else is asked of him: no place, no time, no rank.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ العَظِيمِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
Subḥāna-llāhi-l-ʿAẓīmi wa bi-ḥamdih
Allāh is declared free of every fault, and credited with every good.
سُبْحَانَ — root س ب ح. Subḥān clears Allāh of any defect. The wāw then joins ḥamd to it, so denial and affirmation come together.
غُرِسَتْ لَهُ نَخْلَةٌ فِي الجَنَّةِ
ghurisat lahu nakhlatun fī-l-jannah
The word said here becomes a tree standing there.
غُرِسَتْ — root غ ر س. Ghurisat is passive: planted for him, by someone else. A planted thing takes root and stays.

رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّReported by al-Tirmidhī

قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ قَالَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، فِي يَوْمٍ مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ؛ حُطَّتْ خَطَايَاهُ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ البَحْرِ»

مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍa hundred times

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay a hundred times a day.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
✎Added by us

“Whoever says, ‘Glory be to Allāh, and praise be to Him,’ a hundred times in a day, his sins are wiped away, even if they were like the foam of the sea.”

Man qāla: Subḥāna-llāhi wa bi-ḥamdih, fī yawmin miʾata marrah; ḥuṭṭat khaṭāyāhu wa in kānat mithla zabadi-l-baḥr

مَنْ قَالَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
Man qāla: Subḥāna-llāhi wa bi-ḥamdih
The shortest form of the phrase: glory, then praise.
وَبِحَمْدِهِ — root ح م د. Ḥamd is praise given because the one praised deserves it, not because we want something.
فِي يَوْمٍ مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ
fī yawmin miʾata marrah
The hundred belongs to the day, not to one sitting.
يَوْمٍ — root ي و م. Yawm here is the whole day, so the count can be broken up across it.
حُطَّتْ خَطَايَاهُ
ḥuṭṭat khaṭāyāhu
His sins are taken off him, the way a load is taken off a back.
حُطَّتْ — root ح ط ط. Ḥaṭṭa is to set down a burden you were carrying. The sins are unloaded, not hidden.
وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ البَحْرِ
wa in kānat mithla zabadi-l-baḥr
However many they are, the number is no obstacle.
زَبَدِ — root ز ب د. Zabad is the foam on water: countless small flecks. It is an image of quantity, not of weight.

مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِAgreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

٣
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«أَحَبُّ الكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، لَا يَضُرُّكَ بِأَيِّهِنَّ بَدَأْتَ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay the four in any order you like.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
✎Added by us

“The speech most beloved to Allāh is four: ‘Glory be to Allāh’, ‘praise be to Allāh’, ‘there is no god but Allāh’, and ‘Allāh is greatest’. It does you no harm which of them you begin with.”

Aḥabbu-l-kalāmi ilā-llāhi arbaʿ: Subḥāna-llāh, wa-l-ḥamdu li-llāh, wa lā ilāha illa-llāh, wa-llāhu akbar, lā yaḍurruka bi-ayyihinna badaʾt

سُبْحَانَglory be to

وَاللَّهُand Allāh

لَاit does not
يَضُرُّكَharm you
بِأَيِّهِنَّwith whichever of them
بَدَأْتَyou began
أَحَبُّ الكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ
Aḥabbu-l-kalāmi ilā-llāhi arbaʿ
Out of everything a person can say, four phrases are named as the dearest.
أَحَبُّ — root ح ب ب. Aḥabb is a comparative pushed to the top: most beloved, not merely liked.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
Subḥāna-llāh, wa-l-ḥamdu li-llāh
The first two: He is free of fault, and all praise is His by right.
وَالحَمْدُ — root ح م د. Al-ḥamd carries the definite article: the praise, entire, and the lām in li-llāh assigns it to Him.
وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
wa lā ilāha illa-llāh, wa-llāhu akbar
The third denies every other object of worship; the fourth puts Him above all.
إِلَهَ — root أ ل ه. An ilāh is anything taken as a god. The phrase clears them all away, then names the one that remains.
لَا يَضُرُّكَ بِأَيِّهِنَّ بَدَأْتَ
lā yaḍurruka bi-ayyihinna badaʾt
There is no fixed order; start wherever you like.
بَدَأْتَ — root ب د أ. Badaʾta is 'you began'. The permission is explicit, which spares the beginner any worry about sequence.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ، ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي المِيزَانِ، حَبِيبَتَانِ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ العَظِيمِ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay at any time; short enough to keep on the tongue all day.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ العَظِيمِ
✎Added by us

“Two phrases, light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: ‘Glory be to Allāh, and praise be to Him; glory be to Allāh the Great.’”

Kalimatāni khafīfatāni ʿalā-l-lisān, thaqīlatāni fī-l-mīzān, ḥabībatāni ilā-r-Raḥmān: Subḥāna-llāhi wa bi-ḥamdih, Subḥāna-llāhi-l-ʿAẓīm

عَلَىupon

فِيin
المِيزَانِthe scale
حَبِيبَتَانِbeloved
إِلَىto
الرَّحْمَنِthe Most Merciful

اللَّهِAllāh

سُبْحَانَglory be to
اللَّهِAllāh
العَظِيمِthe Great
كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ
Kalimatāni khafīfatāni ʿalā-l-lisān
Two short phrases that cost the mouth almost nothing.
كَلِمَتَانِ — root ك ل م. Kalimatāni is dual. A kalimah here is a whole phrase, not a single word.
ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي المِيزَانِ
thaqīlatāni fī-l-mīzān
What is cheap to say turns out to be heavy where it counts.
المِيزَانِ — root و ز ن. Al-mīzān is the Scale of the Day of Judgement. Light here, heavy there: the contrast is the whole point.
حَبِيبَتَانِ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ
ḥabībatāni ilā-r-Raḥmān
Allāh Himself loves to hear them.
الرَّحْمَنِ — root ر ح م. Of all His names, ar-Raḥmān is chosen here, the one that speaks of mercy given freely.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ العَظِيمِ
Subḥāna-llāhi wa bi-ḥamdih, Subḥāna-llāhi-l-ʿAẓīm
The two phrases in full: glory with praise, then glory with greatness.
العَظِيمِ — root ع ظ م. Al-ʿAẓīm is the Immense. The second phrase adds His greatness to what the first already said.

مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِAgreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

٥
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«أَيَعْجِزُ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَكْسِبَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ أَلْفَ حَسَنَةٍ؟ فَسَأَلَهُ سَائِلٌ مِنْ جُلَسَائِهِ: كَيْفَ يَكْسِبُ أَحَدُنَا أَلْفَ حَسَنَةٍ؟ قَالَ: يُسَبِّحُ مِئَةَ تَسْبِيحَةٍ؛ فَيُكْتَبُ لَهُ أَلْفُ حَسَنَةٍ، أَوْ يُحَطُّ عَنْهُ أَلْفُ خَطِيئَةٍ»

مِئَةَ تَسْبِيحَةٍa hundred tasbīḥahs

↪ Say subḥāna-llāh a hundred times in the day.

✎Added by us

“Is any of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds every day?” One of those sitting with him asked, “How can one of us earn a thousand good deeds?” He said, “He glorifies Allāh a hundred times, and a thousand good deeds are written for him, or a thousand sins are taken off him.”

A-yaʿjizu aḥadukum an yaksiba kulla yawmin alfa ḥasanah? Fa-saʾalahu sāʾilun min julasāʾih: Kayfa yaksibu aḥadunā alfa ḥasanah? Qāla: Yusabbiḥu miʾata tasbīḥah; fa-yuktabu lahu alfu ḥasanah, aw yuḥaṭṭu ʿanhu alfu khaṭīʾah

تَسْبِيحَةٍglorifications

لَهُfor him

يُحَطُّis put down

خَطِيئَةٍsins
أَيَعْجِزُ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَكْسِبَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ أَلْفَ حَسَنَةٍ
A-yaʿjizu aḥadukum an yaksiba kulla yawmin alfa ḥasanah
He opens with a challenge rather than an instruction.
أَيَعْجِزُ — root ع ج ز. ʿAjaza is to lack the ability. Put as a question, it invites the listener to say no, then to ask how.
فَسَأَلَهُ سَائِلٌ مِنْ جُلَسَائِهِ
Fa-saʾalahu sāʾilun min julasāʾih
The question comes from inside the gathering, not from a stranger.
جُلَسَائِهِ — root ج ل س. Julasāʾ are those who sit with someone regularly. Much of this book was learned in such sittings.
كَيْفَ يَكْسِبُ أَحَدُنَا أَلْفَ حَسَنَةٍ
Kayfa yaksibu aḥadunā alfa ḥasanah
He asks for the method, having accepted the amount.
يَكْسِبُ — root ك س ب. Kasaba is to earn by working. The man assumes labour; the answer will be words.
قَالَ: يُسَبِّحُ مِئَةَ تَسْبِيحَةٍ
Qāla: Yusabbiḥu miʾata tasbīḥah
The whole method is one phrase, said a hundred times.
يُسَبِّحُ — root س ب ح. Yusabbiḥu is Form II: to say subḥāna-llāh. Tasbīḥah is one single utterance of it.
فَيُكْتَبُ لَهُ أَلْفُ حَسَنَةٍ، أَوْ يُحَطُّ عَنْهُ أَلْفُ خَطِيئَةٍ
fa-yuktabu lahu alfu ḥasanah, aw yuḥaṭṭu ʿanhu alfu khaṭīʾah
Either a thousand are added to his credit or a thousand are taken off his debt.
يُحَطُّ — root ح ط ط. Yuḥaṭṭu is 'is set down', the same word used for lifting a load. Each tasbīḥah counts ten either way.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

٦
عَنْ جُوَيْرِيَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَاFrom Juwayriyah (may Allāh be pleased with her)
الكِتَابFrom the book

«أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ خَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا بُكْرَةً حِينَ صَلَّى الصُّبْحَ، وَهِيَ فِي مَسْجِدِهَا. ثُمَّ رَجَعَ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَضْحَى، وَهِيَ جَالِسَةٌ، فَقَالَ: مَا زِلْتِ عَلَى الحَالِ الَّتِي فَارَقْتُكِ عَلَيْهَا؟ قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ. قَالَ: لَقَدْ قُلْتُ بَعْدَكِ أَرْبَعَ كَلِمَاتٍ - ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ -، لَوْ وُزِنَتْ بِمَا قُلْتِ مُنْذُ اليَوْمِ لَوَزَنَتْهُنَّ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ، وَرِضَا نَفْسِهِ، وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ، وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ»

ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍthree times

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay three times; one round can outweigh a whole morning of dhikr.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ، وَرِضَا نَفْسِهِ، وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ، وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ
✎Added by us

That the Prophet ﷺ left her early in the day, having prayed Ṣubḥ, while she was at her place of prayer. Then he came back after the forenoon had set in, and she was still sitting there. He said, “Have you stayed in the same state I left you in?” She said, “Yes.” He said, “Since leaving you I have said four phrases, three times, which — were they weighed against everything you have said since morning — would outweigh them: ‘Glory be to Allāh, and praise be to Him: as many as the number of His creation, as much as pleases Him, as heavy as the weight of His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words.’”

Anna-n-Nabiyya ﷺ kharaja min ʿindihā bukratan ḥīna ṣallā-ṣ-Ṣubḥ, wa hiya fī masjidihā. Thumma rajaʿa baʿda an aḍḥā, wa hiya jālisah, fa-qāla: Mā zilti ʿalā-l-ḥāli-llatī fāraqtuki ʿalayhā? Qālat: Naʿam. Qāla: La-qad qultu baʿdaki arbaʿa kalimātin, thalātha marrātin, law wuzinat bimā qulti mundhu-l-yawmi la-wazanat-hunn: Subḥāna-llāhi wa bi-ḥamdih, ʿadada khalqih, wa riḍā nafsih, wa zinata ʿarshih, wa midāda kalimātih

أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ خَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا بُكْرَةً حِينَ صَلَّى الصُّبْحَ، وَهِيَ فِي مَسْجِدِهَا
Anna-n-Nabiyya ﷺ kharaja min ʿindihā bukratan ḥīna ṣallā-ṣ-Ṣubḥ, wa hiya fī masjidihā
He leaves at first light after the dawn prayer; she stays where she prays at home.
مَسْجِدِهَا — The book explains masjidihā as her place of prayer inside her house (root س ج د). A woman's masjid can be a corner of a room.
ثُمَّ رَجَعَ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَضْحَى، وَهِيَ جَالِسَةٌ
Thumma rajaʿa baʿda an aḍḥā, wa hiya jālisah
Hours pass. He comes back mid-morning and finds her exactly as before.
أَضْحَى — The book explains aḍḥā as: he entered the time of ḍuḥā, the forenoon (root ض ح و). It marks how long she had sat.
فَقَالَ: مَا زِلْتِ عَلَى الحَالِ الَّتِي فَارَقْتُكِ عَلَيْهَا؟ قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ
fa-qāla: Mā zilti ʿalā-l-ḥāli-llatī fāraqtuki ʿalayhā? Qālat: Naʿam
He checks whether she has really been at it the whole time, and she confirms.
فَارَقْتُكِ — root ف ر ق. Fāraqtuki is 'I parted from you'. The word measures the gap between his leaving and his return.
قَالَ: لَقَدْ قُلْتُ بَعْدَكِ أَرْبَعَ كَلِمَاتٍ - ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ
Qāla: La-qad qultu baʿdaki arbaʿa kalimātin, thalātha marrātin
Against her long morning he sets four phrases, said three times over.
كَلِمَاتٍ — root ك ل م. Kalimah here means a phrase, not a word: four clauses, each beginning with a comparison.
لَوْ وُزِنَتْ بِمَا قُلْتِ مُنْذُ اليَوْمِ لَوَزَنَتْهُنَّ
law wuzinat bimā qulti mundhu-l-yawmi la-wazanat-hunn
Put on a scale against everything she said, the four phrases weigh more.
لَوَزَنَتْهُنَّ — root و ز ن. Wazana is to weigh and to outweigh. The measure is weight, not length of time.
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ، وَرِضَا نَفْسِهِ، وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ، وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ
Subḥāna-llāhi wa bi-ḥamdih, ʿadada khalqih, wa riḍā nafsih, wa zinata ʿarshih, wa midāda kalimātih
Glory and praise, then four measures: His creation, His pleasure, His Throne, His words.
وَمِدَادَ — The book explains midāda kalimātih as: the amount that matches them in number and abundance (root م د د). Each measure is beyond counting.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
بُكْرَةًأَيْ: أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ
bukratan — early in the morningThat is: the first part of the day.
مَسْجِدِهَاأَيْ: مَكَانِ صَلَاتِهَا فِي بَيْتِهَا
masjidihā — her place of prayerThat is: the place of her prayer in her house.
أَضْحَىأَيْ: دَخَلَ فِي وَقْتِ الضُّحَى
aḍḥā — he reached the forenoonThat is: he entered the time of the forenoon.
مِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِأَيْ: قَدْرَ مَا يُوَازِيهَا فِي العَدَدِ وَالكَثْرَةِ
midāda kalimātihi — as much as the ink of His wordsThat is: the amount that matches them in number and abundance.

«٦١» · General Adhkār

التَّهْلِيلُ

Chapter 61 — Declaring Allāh's Oneness

Book p.146 · أَذْكَارٌ عَامَّةٌ — General Adhkār · 2 entries in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، فِي يَوْمٍ مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ. كَانَتْ لَهُ عَدْلَ عَشْرِ رِقَابٍ، وَكُتِبَتْ لَهُ مِئَةُ حَسَنَةٍ، وَمُحِيَتْ عَنْهُ مِئَةُ سَيِّئَةٍ. وَكَانَتْ لَهُ حِرْزاً مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ يَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُمْسِيَ. وَلَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ بِأَفْضَلَ مِمَّا جَاءَ بِهِ؛ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ عَمِلَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ»

مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍa hundred times

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay a hundred times in the day.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
✎Added by us

“Whoever says, ‘There is no god but Allāh alone, He has no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things,’ a hundred times in a day, he has the equal of freeing ten slaves, a hundred good deeds are written for him, a hundred bad deeds are wiped from him, and it is a guard for him against Satan for that day of his until evening. And no one brings anything better than what he has brought, except a man who does more than that.”

Man qāla: Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahu-l-mulk, wa lahu-l-ḥamd, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr, fī yawmin miʾata marrah. Kānat lahu ʿadla ʿashri riqāb, wa kutibat lahu miʾatu ḥasanah, wa muḥiyat ʿanhu miʾatu sayyiʾah. Wa kānat lahu ḥirzan mina-sh-shayṭāni yawmahu dhālika ḥattā yumsī. Wa lam yaʾti aḥadun bi-afḍala mimmā jāʾa bih; illā rajulun ʿamila akthara min dhālik

مَنْ قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ
Man qāla: Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah
One God, by Himself, with nobody sharing the position.
وَحْدَهُ — root و ح د. Waḥdahu means He is alone in it. The clause that follows says the same thing again from the other side: no partner.
لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
lahu-l-mulk, wa lahu-l-ḥamd, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr
Ownership is His, praise is His, and His power covers everything without exception.
المُلْكُ — root م ل ك. Mulk is ownership joined to authority: not just holding a thing but disposing of it as one wills.
فِي يَوْمٍ مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ
fī yawmin miʾata marrah
A hundred in the course of a day, not a hundred at one sitting.
مَرَّةٍ — root م ر ر. Marrah is a single instance. Counting by instances lets the hundred be spread out.
كَانَتْ لَهُ عَدْلَ عَشْرِ رِقَابٍ، وَكُتِبَتْ لَهُ مِئَةُ حَسَنَةٍ، وَمُحِيَتْ عَنْهُ مِئَةُ سَيِّئَةٍ
Kānat lahu ʿadla ʿashri riqāb, wa kutibat lahu miʾatu ḥasanah, wa muḥiyat ʿanhu miʾatu sayyiʾah
It weighs as much as ten freed slaves, and it moves the record in both directions at once.
عَدْلَ — The book explains ʿadla ʿashri riqāb as: he has the like of the reward of freeing ten slaves (root ع د ل, equal weight). Riqāb is literally 'necks'.
وَكَانَتْ لَهُ حِرْزاً مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ يَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُمْسِيَ
Wa kānat lahu ḥirzan mina-sh-shayṭāni yawmahu dhālika ḥattā yumsī
For the rest of that day it stands between him and Satan.
حِرْزاً — The book explains ḥirzan simply as ḥifẓan, protection (root ح ر ز). A ḥirz is a fortified place you get inside of.
وَلَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ بِأَفْضَلَ مِمَّا جَاءَ بِهِ؛ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ عَمِلَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
Wa lam yaʾti aḥadun bi-afḍala mimmā jāʾa bih; illā rajulun ʿamila akthara min dhālik
Nothing better is brought that day, and the only way to beat it is to say more of it.
بِأَفْضَلَ — root ف ض ل. Afḍal is 'more excellent'. The exception is telling: quantity of the same dhikr, not some other deed.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
عَدْلَ عَشْرِ رِقَابٍأَيْ: لَهُ مِثْلُ ثَوَابِ عِتْقِ عَشَرَةٍ مِنَ العَبِيدِ
ʿadla ʿashri riqāb — the equivalent of ten slavesThat is: he has the like of the reward of freeing ten slaves.
حِرْزاًأَيْ: حِفْظاً
ḥirzan — a protectionThat is: a safeguard.

مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِAgreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

٢
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، عَشْرَ مِرَارٍ؛ كَانَ كَمَنْ أَعْتَقَ أَرْبَعَةَ أَنْفُسٍ مِنْ وَلَدِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ»

عَشْرَ مِرَارٍten times

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay ten times.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
✎Added by us

“Whoever says, ‘There is no god but Allāh alone, He has no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things,’ ten times, he is like one who has freed four souls from the children of Ismāʿīl.”

Man qāla: Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahu-l-mulk, wa lahu-l-ḥamd, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr, ʿashra mirār; kāna ka-man aʿtaqa arbaʿata anfusin min waladi Ismāʿīl

مَنْ قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ
Man qāla: Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah
The same phrase as the hadith before, opening with the denial of any partner.
شَرِيكَ — root ش ر ك. A sharīk is a business partner with a stake. Denying Him one is the plainest statement of tawḥīd.
لَهُ المُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
lahu-l-mulk, wa lahu-l-ḥamd, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr
What He owns, what He deserves, and what He can do: all three are total.
قَدِيرٌ — root ق د ر. Qadīr is the intensive form of qādir, one who has power. Paired with 'every thing', it leaves no gap.
عَشْرَ مِرَارٍ؛ كَانَ كَمَنْ أَعْتَقَ أَرْبَعَةَ أَنْفُسٍ مِنْ وَلَدِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ
ʿashra mirār; kāna ka-man aʿtaqa arbaʿata anfusin min waladi Ismāʿīl
Ten times is enough to match the freeing of four people of noble descent.
أَعْتَقَ — root ع ت ق. Aʿtaqa is to set a slave free. The book notes that the children of Ismāʿīl are named here because of their honour over others.

waladi Ismāʿīl — the children of IsmāʿīlHe singled them out because of their nobility over others.

١

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay when a task feels beyond you.

✎Added by us

“Shall I not point you to a phrase that is a treasure among the treasures of Paradise? ‘There is no capacity and no power except by Allāh.’”

Alā adulluka ʿalā kalimatin hiya kanzun min kunūzi-l-jannah?! Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā bi-llāh

Alā adulluka ʿalā kalimatin hiya
He offers it as a question, the way you offer someone a gift.
أَدُلُّكَ — root د ل ل. Adulluka is to guide someone to a thing they would not have found alone. The alā at the front softens it into an invitation.
كَنْزٌ مِنْ كُنُوزِ الجَنَّةِ
kanzun min kunūzi-l-jannah
Something stored away now, collected later.
كَنْزٌ — The book explains it as: a precious reward laid up in Paradise for whoever says it (root ك ن ز). A kanz is buried wealth.
لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā bi-llāh
No ability to change a thing, and no strength to act, except from Him.
حَوْلَ — root ح و ل. Ḥawl is the capacity to turn a situation around; quwwah is the strength to carry it through. Both are denied to us and traced back to Allāh.

Chapter 63 — Seeking Forgiveness and Turning Back to Allāh

Book p.149 · أَذْكَارٌ عَامَّةٌ — General Adhkār · 3 entries in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«إِنِّي لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ فِي اليَوْمِ - مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ -»

مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍa hundred times

↪ Ask forgiveness a hundred times a day, as he did.

✎Added by us

“I seek Allāh's forgiveness a hundred times in the day.”

Innī la-astaghfiru-llāha fī-l-yawmi miʾata marrah

إِنِّيindeed I
لَأَسْتَغْفِرُdo seek the forgiveness of
اللَّهَAllāh
فِيin
اليَوْمِthe day
مِئَةَa hundred
مَرَّةٍtimes
إِنِّي لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ
Innī la-astaghfiru-llāha
He speaks about himself, and with emphasis.
لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ — root غ ف ر, Form X. Istighfār is asking for a fault to be covered over. Inna plus the lām make the statement as strong as Arabic can make it.
فِي اليَوْمِ - مِئَةَ مَرَّةٍ
fī-l-yawmi miʾata marrah
A hundred is his daily figure, and he had nothing to be forgiven for.
اليَوْمِ — root ي و م. The definite al-yawm means the day as such, that is, every day. It sets the floor, not the ceiling, for the rest of us.

٢
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يُذْنِبُ ذَنْباً، فَيَتَوَضَّأُ، فَيُحْسِنُ الوُضُوءَ، ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ، فَيَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ ﷻ؛ إِلَّا غَفَرَ لَهُ»

↪ After a sin: wuḍūʾ, two rakʿahs, then ask forgiveness.

✎Added by us

“There is no man who commits a sin, then performs wuḍūʾ and performs it well, then prays two rakʿahs, then asks Allāh ﷻ for forgiveness, except that He forgives him.”

Mā min rajulin yudhnibu dhanban, fa-yatawaḍḍaʾu, fa-yuḥsinu-l-wuḍūʾa, thumma yuṣallī rakʿatayn, fa-yastaghfiru-llāha ﷻ; illā ghafara lah

مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يُذْنِبُ ذَنْباً
Mā min rajulin yudhnibu dhanban
It begins by taking the sin as given, not by scolding.
يُذْنِبُ — root ذ ن ب. A dhanb is a fault that trails behind a person, from the same root as dhanab, a tail.
فَيَتَوَضَّأُ، فَيُحْسِنُ الوُضُوءَ، ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ
fa-yatawaḍḍaʾu, fa-yuḥsinu-l-wuḍūʾa, thumma yuṣallī rakʿatayn
Three steps, in order: wash, wash properly, then pray two short units.
فَيُحْسِنُ — root ح س ن, Form IV. Iḥsān is doing a thing well, not merely doing it. Doing the wuḍūʾ well is written into the condition.
فَيَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ ﷻ؛ إِلَّا غَفَرَ لَهُ
fa-yastaghfiru-llāha ﷻ; illā ghafara lah
Then he asks, and the forgiveness follows.
غَفَرَ — root غ ف ر. Ghafara is to cover over. The mā... illā frame makes this certain rather than likely: there is no such man except that he is forgiven.

“O people, turn back to Allāh in repentance, for I turn back to Him a hundred times in the day.”

تُوبُوا — root ت و ب. Tawbah is literally a return. The preposition ilā fixes the direction, so it is not just regret but a going back.

Chapter 64 — When the Wind Blows Hard

Book p.152 · الرِّيحُ وَالمَطَرُ — Wind & Rain · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا عَصَفَتِ الرِّيحُ قَالَWhen the wind blew hard the Prophet ﷺ would say
الكِتَابFrom the book

«اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَهَا، وَخَيْرَ مَا فِيهَا، وَخَيْرَ مَا أُرْسِلَتْ بِهِ. وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا، وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهَا، وَشَرِّ مَا أُرْسِلَتْ بِهِ»

↪ Say when the wind picks up.

✎Added by us

“O Allāh, I ask You for its good, the good that is in it, and the good it was sent with. And I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil that is in it, and the evil it was sent with.”

Allāhumma innī asʾaluka khayrahā, wa khayra mā fīhā, wa khayra mā ursilat bih. Wa aʿūdhu bika min sharrihā, wa sharri mā fīhā, wa sharri mā ursilat bih

اللَّهُمَّO Allāh
إِنِّيindeed I
أَسْأَلُكَask You for

وَخَيْرَand the good of

مَاwhat

مِنْfrom

اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَهَا
Allāhumma innī asʾaluka khayrahā
The first move is to ask for the wind's own good, not to complain about it.
أَسْأَلُكَ — root س ء ل. Asʾaluka is to ask, and the object here is khayr. A strong wind is met with a request, not a protest.
وَخَيْرَ مَا فِيهَا، وَخَيْرَ مَا أُرْسِلَتْ بِهِ
wa khayra mā fīhā, wa khayra mā ursilat bih
Three layers: the wind itself, whatever it carries, and the errand it came on.
أُرْسِلَتْ — root ر س ل, passive. Ursilat means it was sent. The wind has a Sender, so the book's gloss on ʿaṣafat, that it blew hard, describes force under command.
وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا
Wa aʿūdhu bika min sharrihā
Then the other half: shelter from what it may bring.
وَأَعُوذُ — root ع و ذ. To seek ʿiyādh is to run to someone stronger and stand behind them.
وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهَا، وَشَرِّ مَا أُرْسِلَتْ بِهِ
wa sharri mā fīhā, wa sharri mā ursilat bih
The same three layers again, asked against instead of asked for.
وَشَرِّ — root ش ر ر. The second half mirrors the first word for word, with sharr in place of khayr. Learning one half gives you both.

Chapter 65 — When Rain Falls

Book p.153 · الرِّيحُ وَالمَطَرُ — Wind & Rain · 2 entries in the printed text.

١
كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا رَأَى المَطَرَ قَالَWhen the Prophet ﷺ saw rain he would say
الكِتَابFrom the book

«اللَّهُمَّ صَيِّباً نَافِعاً»

↪ Say on seeing rain.

✎Added by us

“O Allāh, a heavy and beneficial rain.”

Allāhumma ṣayyiban nāfiʿan

اللَّهُمَّO Allāh
صَيِّباًa heavy downpour
نَافِعاًbeneficial
اللَّهُمَّ
Allāhumma
The duʿāʾ is two words long, and it starts by calling on Him.
اللَّهُمَّ — root أ ل ه. Allāhumma is the vocative of Allāh with a mīm added at the end in place of yā at the front.
صَيِّباً نَافِعاً
ṣayyiban nāfiʿan
Not rain for its own sake, but rain that does good.
صَيِّباً — The book explains ṣayyiban as abundant rain (root ص و ب, to come down). Nāfiʿan then qualifies it: plenty that helps, since plenty can also ruin.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
صَيِّباًأَيْ: مَطَراً كَثِيراً
ṣayyiban — a heavy downpourThat is: abundant rain.

رَوَاهُ البُخَارِيُّReported by al-Bukhārī

٢
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«قَالَ اللَّهُ ﷻ: أَصْبَحَ مِنْ عِبَادِي مُؤْمِنٌ بِي وَكَافِرٌ: فَأَمَّا مَنْ قَالَ: مُطِرْنَا بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَرَحْمَتِهِ؛ فَذَلِكَ مُؤْمِنٌ بِي كَافِرٌ بِالكَوْكَبِ. وَأَمَّا مَنْ قَالَ: مُطِرْنَا بِنَوْءِ كَذَا وَكَذَا؛ فَذَلِكَ كَافِرٌ بِي مُؤْمِنٌ بِالكَوْكَبِ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay after rain, crediting Allāh rather than the weather.
مُطِرْنَا بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَرَحْمَتِهِ
✎Added by us

“Allāh ﷻ said: ‘Among My servants, morning has come upon one who believes in Me and one who disbelieves. As for the one who says, “We were given rain by the bounty of Allāh and His mercy,” that one believes in Me and disbelieves in the star. And as for the one who says, “We were given rain by the rising of such and such a star,” that one disbelieves in Me and believes in the star.’”

Qāla-llāhu ﷻ: Aṣbaḥa min ʿibādī muʾminun bī wa kāfir: fa-ammā man qāla: Muṭirnā bi-faḍli-llāhi wa raḥmatih; fa-dhālika muʾminun bī kāfirun bi-l-kawkab. Wa ammā man qāla: Muṭirnā bi-nawʾi kadhā wa kadhā; fa-dhālika kāfirun bī muʾminun bi-l-kawkab

مُؤْمِنٌbelieving
بِالكَوْكَبِin the star
قَالَ اللَّهُ ﷻ: أَصْبَحَ مِنْ عِبَادِي مُؤْمِنٌ بِي وَكَافِرٌ
Qāla-llāhu ﷻ: Aṣbaḥa min ʿibādī muʾminun bī wa kāfir
The same rain falls on two people, and by morning they are not in the same state.
عِبَادِي — root ع ب د. Both are called ʿibādī, My servants. What separates them is only what they say next.
فَأَمَّا مَنْ قَالَ: مُطِرْنَا بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَرَحْمَتِهِ
fa-ammā man qāla: Muṭirnā bi-faḍli-llāhi wa raḥmatih
The first names the giver: this came from His bounty and His mercy.
مُطِرْنَا — root م ط ر, passive. Muṭirnā is 'we were rained upon': the rain is something done to us, and the bi- names who did it.
فَذَلِكَ مُؤْمِنٌ بِي كَافِرٌ بِالكَوْكَبِ
fa-dhālika muʾminun bī kāfirun bi-l-kawkab
Crediting Allāh is at the same time a refusal to credit anything else.
كَافِرٌ — root ك ف ر. Kufr is covering up or refusing to acknowledge. Here it is used approvingly: he refuses to acknowledge the star.
وَأَمَّا مَنْ قَالَ: مُطِرْنَا بِنَوْءِ كَذَا وَكَذَا؛ فَذَلِكَ كَافِرٌ بِي مُؤْمِنٌ بِالكَوْكَبِ
Wa ammā man qāla: Muṭirnā bi-nawʾi kadhā wa kadhā; fa-dhālika kāfirun bī muʾminun bi-l-kawkab
The second gives the credit to a star, and the two verdicts swap places.
بِنَوْءِ — The book explains bi-nawʾi kadhā wa kadhā as: because of the rising of such and such a star (root ن و ء). Naming a cause instead of the Causer is what is condemned.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
بِنَوْءِ كَذَا وَكَذَاأَيْ: بِسَبَبِ طُلُوعِ النَّجْمِ الفُلَانِيِّ
bi-nawʾi kadhā wa-kadhā — by such-and-such a starThat is: because of the rising of such-and-such a star.

مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِAgreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

Chapter 66 — Hearing a Cockerel Crow and a Donkey Bray

Book p.156 · سَمَاعُ صِيَاحِ الدِّيكِ وَنَهِيقِ الحِمَارِ — Cockerel & Donkey · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ صِيَاحَ الدِّيَكَةِ: فَاسْأَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ؛ فَإِنَّهَا رَأَتْ مَلَكاً. وَإِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ نَهِيقَ الحِمَارِ: فَتَعَوَّذُوا بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ رَأَى شَيْطَاناً»

↪ Ask at the cockerel's crow; seek refuge at the donkey's bray.

✎Added by us

“When you hear cockerels crowing, ask Allāh of His bounty, for it has seen an angel. And when you hear a donkey braying, seek refuge in Allāh from Satan, for it has seen a devil.”

Idhā samiʿtum ṣiyāḥa-d-diyakah: fa-sʾalū-llāha min faḍlih; fa-innahā raʾat malakan. Wa idhā samiʿtum nahīqa-l-ḥimār: fa-taʿawwadhū bi-llāhi mina-sh-shayṭān; fa-innahu raʾā shayṭānan

الحِمَارِthe donkey
فَتَعَوَّذُواthen seek refuge
بِاللَّهِin Allāh
مِنَfrom
الشَّيْطَانِSatan
فَإِنَّهُfor it
رَأَىhas seen
شَيْطَاناًa devil
إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ صِيَاحَ الدِّيَكَةِ
Idhā samiʿtum ṣiyāḥa-d-diyakah
An ordinary farmyard sound is made into a signal.
صِيَاحَ — root ص ي ح. Ṣiyāḥ is a loud call or shout. Ad-diyakah is the plural of dīk, a cockerel.
فَاسْأَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ؛ فَإِنَّهَا رَأَتْ مَلَكاً
fa-sʾalū-llāha min faḍlih; fa-innahā raʾat malakan
Ask, and the reason given is that the bird has seen an angel.
فَضْلِهِ — root ف ض ل. Faḍl is what Allāh gives beyond anything owed. The moment an angel is near is a good moment to ask.
وَإِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ نَهِيقَ الحِمَارِ
Wa idhā samiʿtum nahīqa-l-ḥimār
The second sound, and the opposite instruction.
نَهِيقَ — The book explains nahīq simply as its voice, the sound a donkey makes (root ن ه ق).
فَتَعَوَّذُوا بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ رَأَى شَيْطَاناً
fa-taʿawwadhū bi-llāhi mina-sh-shayṭān; fa-innahu raʾā shayṭānan
Here you take shelter instead of asking, because of what the donkey has seen.
فَتَعَوَّذُوا — root ع و ذ, Form V. Taʿawwadhū is to take shelter with Allāh. Two sounds, two reasons, two different responses.

Chapter 67 — Stopping at a Place to Stay

Book p.158 · المُخَالَطَةُ — Mixing with People · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«مَنْ نَزَلَ مَنْزِلاً، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ؛ لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ شَيْءٌ حَتَّى يَرْتَحِلَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ ذَلِكَ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay when you stop anywhere to rest or stay.
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
✎Added by us

“Whoever stops at a place and then says, ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allāh from the evil of what He has created,’ nothing will harm him until he moves on from that place of his.”

Man nazala manzilan, thumma qāla: Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq; lam yaḍurruhu shayʾun ḥattā yartaḥila min manzilihi dhālik

Man nazala manzilan, thumma qāla
Any stop counts, and the words come after settling in.
مَنْزِلاً — The book explains manzil simply as a place (root ن ز ل). A house, a camp, a hotel room, a roadside halt.
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq
Refuge is taken in Allāh's own words, against harm from anything He made.
التَّامَّاتِ — root ت م م. Tāmmāt means complete, with nothing lacking. Because His words fall short in nothing, refuge in them does not fail.
لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ شَيْءٌ حَتَّى يَرْتَحِلَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ ذَلِكَ
lam yaḍurruhu shayʾun ḥattā yartaḥila min manzilihi dhālik
The safety lasts exactly as long as the stay.
يَرْتَحِلَ — root ر ح ل, Form VIII. Yartaḥil is to move on from a halting place. So the duʿāʾ is repeated at each new stop.

Chapter 68 — What to Say When You Love Someone for Allāh's Sake

Book p.159 · المُخَالَطَةُ — Mixing with People · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُAnas ibn Mālik (may Allāh be pleased with him) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كُنْتُ جَالِساً عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذْ مَرَّ رَجُلٌ. فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ القَوْمِ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ. قَالَ: هَلْ أَعْلَمْتَهُ ذَلِكَ؟ قَالَ: لَا. قَالَ: قُمْ فَأَعْلِمْهُ. قَالَ: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: يَا هَذَا، وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّكَ فِي اللَّهِ. قَالَ: أَحَبَّكَ الَّذِي أَحْبَبْتَنِي لَهُ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay it to the person you love. He answers: أَحَبَّكَ الَّذِي أَحْبَبْتَنِي لَهُ — “May the One for whose sake you loved me love you.”
إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّكَ فِي اللَّهِ
✎Added by us

I was sitting with the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ when a man passed by. A man from the gathering said, “O Messenger of Allāh, I truly love this man.” He said, “Have you told him so?” He said, “No.” He said, “Get up and tell him.” So he went over to him and said, “You there, by Allāh, I love you for Allāh's sake.” He replied, “May the One for whose sake you loved me love you.”

Kuntu jālisan ʿinda Rasūli-llāhi ﷺ idh marra rajul. Fa-qāla rajulun mina-l-qawm: Yā Rasūla-llāh, innī la-uḥibbu hādha-r-rajul. Qāla: Hal aʿlamtahu dhālik? Qāla: Lā. Qāla: Qum fa-aʿlimh. Qāla: Fa-qāma ilayh, fa-qāla: Yā hādhā, wa-llāhi innī la-uḥibbuka fī-llāh. Qāla: Aḥabbaka-lladhī aḥbabtanī lah

كُنْتُ جَالِساً عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذْ مَرَّ رَجُلٌ
Kuntu jālisan ʿinda Rasūli-llāhi ﷺ idh marra rajul
Anas is in the Prophet's company when a man walks past. Nothing unusual so far.
جَالِساً — root ج ل س. Jālisan is 'sitting'. A great deal of this book was learned by Companions simply sitting where he sat.
فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ القَوْمِ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ
Fa-qāla rajulun mina-l-qawm: Yā Rasūla-llāh, innī la-uḥibbu hādha-r-rajul
Someone in the gathering says out loud that he loves the man who just passed.
لَأُحِبُّ — root ح ب ب. The lām on la-uḥibbu is emphatic: he is not saying he thinks well of him, he is saying he loves him.
قَالَ: هَلْ أَعْلَمْتَهُ ذَلِكَ؟ قَالَ: لَا. قَالَ: قُمْ فَأَعْلِمْهُ
Qāla: Hal aʿlamtahu dhālik? Qāla: Lā. Qāla: Qum fa-aʿlimh
The Prophet ﷺ asks whether the man knows, then tells him to go and say so.
أَعْلَمْتَهُ — root ع ل م, Form IV. Aʿlama is to make someone know a thing. Love the other person never hears about does him no good.
قَالَ: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: يَا هَذَا، وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّكَ فِي اللَّهِ
Qāla: Fa-qāma ilayh, fa-qāla: Yā hādhā, wa-llāhi innī la-uḥibbuka fī-llāh
He acts at once, walks over, and says it plainly with Allāh named as the reason.
فَقَامَ — root ق و م. Fa-qāma, 'so he stood up': the fā indicates he did it straight away, not later.
قَالَ: أَحَبَّكَ الَّذِي أَحْبَبْتَنِي لَهُ
Qāla: Aḥabbaka-lladhī aḥbabtanī lah
The man answers with a duʿāʾ instead of an embarrassed thank-you.
أَحَبَّكَ — root ح ب ب appears three times in this one line. Love offered for Allāh's sake is answered by asking Allāh to return it.

رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُReported by Aḥmad

Book p.160 · المُخَالَطَةُ — Mixing with People · 1 entry in the printed text.

↪ Ask for blessing on him the moment you admire something of his.

The frame is set before the ruling: this is a brother, not a rival.
أَخِيهِ — root أ خ و. Akhīhi, 'his brother', is how believers are named throughout. It rules out envy before the sentence finishes.

mā yuʿjibuh
The moment addressed is the moment of admiration.

fa-l-yadʿu lahu bi-l-barakah
Turn the admiration outward: ask for good to stay with him.
بِالبَرَكَةِ — root ب ر ك. Barakah is good that settles and increases. Asking for it makes the glance a gift instead of a threat.

Chapter 71 — Responding to One Who Sneezes

Book p.162 · المُخَالَطَةُ — Mixing with People · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«إِذَا عَطَسَ أَحَدُكُمْ؛ فَلْيَقُلِ: الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. وَلْيَقُلْ لَهُ أَخُوهُ - أَوْ: صَاحِبُهُ -: يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ. فَإِذَا قَالَ لَهُ: يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ. فَلْيَقُلْ: يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُ، وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَكُمْ»

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay this when you sneeze. Whoever hears it answers يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ, and the sneezer then replies يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُ، وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَكُمْ.
الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
✎Added by us

“When one of you sneezes, let him say, ‘Praise be to Allāh.’ And let his brother, or his companion, say to him, ‘May Allāh have mercy on you.’ And when he says to him, ‘May Allāh have mercy on you,’ let him reply, ‘May Allāh guide you and set your affairs right.’”

Idhā ʿaṭasa aḥadukum; fa-l-yaquli: Al-ḥamdu li-llāh. Wa-l-yaqul lahu akhūhu — aw: ṣāḥibuhu —: Yarḥamuka-llāh. Fa-idhā qāla lahu: Yarḥamuka-llāh. Fa-l-yaqul: Yahdīkumu-llāhu, wa-yuṣliḥu bālakum

يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُmay Allāh guide you
وَيُصْلِحُand set right
بَالَكُمْyour state
إِذَا عَطَسَ أَحَدُكُمْ؛ فَلْيَقُلِ: الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
Idhā ʿaṭasa aḥadukum; fa-l-yaquli: Al-ḥamdu li-llāh
A sneeze is met first with praise, and by the one who sneezed.
عَطَسَ — root ع ط س. ʿAṭasa is the plain verb for sneezing. Nothing is asked of the sneezer except that he praise Allāh.
وَلْيَقُلْ لَهُ أَخُوهُ - أَوْ: صَاحِبُهُ -: يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ
Wa-l-yaqul lahu akhūhu — aw: ṣāḥibuhu —: Yarḥamuka-llāh
Whoever hears him owes him a prayer for mercy in return.
أَخُوهُ — root أ خ و. Akhūhu is 'his brother'. The alternative, ṣāḥibuhu, 'his companion', widens it to anyone sitting nearby.
فَإِذَا قَالَ لَهُ: يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ. فَلْيَقُلْ
Fa-idhā qāla lahu: Yarḥamuka-llāh. Fa-l-yaqul
The exchange does not stop there; the sneezer owes a reply of his own.
فَلْيَقُلْ — root ق و ل, with the lām of command. Fa-l-yaqul makes the answer an instruction, not a courtesy.
يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُ، وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَكُمْ
Yahdīkumu-llāhu, wa-yuṣliḥu bālakum
He asks for more than he was given: guidance, and the setting right of a whole life.
بَالَكُمْ — root ب و ل. The book glosses it: your state. So the prayer reaches past the moment to everything a person is dealing with.

الكِتَاب ✎Book's words, our extraction
قُلْSay this the moment you feel anger rising.
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
✎Added by us

Two men traded insults in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and one of them grew angry until his face went red. The Prophet ﷺ looked at him and said: “I know a word which, if he said it, would take this away from him: ‘I seek refuge with Allāh from Satan the accursed.’”

Istabba rajulāni ʿinda-n-Nabiyyi ﷺ, fa-jaʿala aḥaduhumā yaghḍabu wa-yaḥmarru wajhuh. Fa-naẓara ilayhi-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ, fa-qāla: Innī la-aʿlamu kalimatan law qālahā la-dhahaba dhā ʿanh: Aʿūdhu bi-llāhi mina-sh-Shayṭāni-r-Rajīm

Two men fell to insulting each other, and they did it in front of him.
اسْتَبَّ — root س ب ب, Form VIII. The book explains what took place: abuse passed between the two of them, each answering the other.
فَجَعَلَ أَحَدُهُمَا يَغْضَبُ وَيَحْمَرُّ وَجْهُهُ
fa-jaʿala aḥaduhumā yaghḍabu wa-yaḥmarru wajhuh
One of them was losing hold of himself, and it showed.
وَيَحْمَرُّ — root ح م ر. The verb form describes a colour coming on by degrees. The anger had reached his skin.
فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ، فَقَالَ
Fa-naẓara ilayhi-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ, fa-qāla
The Prophet ﷺ watched him first, then spoke.
فَنَظَرَ — root ن ظ ر. He looked before he taught, so the remedy is offered to a man in the middle of it.
إِنِّي لَأَعْلَمُ كَلِمَةً لَوْ قَالَهَا لَذَهَبَ ذَا عَنْهُ
Innī la-aʿlamu kalimatan law qālahā la-dhahaba dhā ʿanh
He says one short phrase would carry the whole of it off.
كَلِمَةً — root ك ل م. A kalimah is a word or brief phrase. The cure named is that small.
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
Aʿūdhu bi-llāhi mina-sh-Shayṭāni-r-Rajīm
The phrase itself: taking shelter with Allāh from the one stirring it up.
أَعُوذُ — root ع و ذ. To seek ʿiyādhah is to run to someone stronger for cover. Anger is treated here as an attack from outside.

Book p.164 · المُخَالَطَةُ — Mixing with People · 1 entry in the printed text.

مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي مَجْلِسٍ، فَكَثُرَ فِيهِ لَغَطُهُ
Man jalasa fī majlisin, fa-kathura fīhi laghaṭuh
The case described is an ordinary sitting that filled up with talk of no value.
لَغَطُهُ — root ل غ ط. The book glosses it: speech that brings no benefit. Not necessarily sin, just noise.
فَقَالَ - قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقُومَ مِنْ مَجْلِسِهِ ذَلِكَ
fa-qāla — qabla an yaqūma min majlisihi dhālika
The remedy has a deadline attached: say it before you stand up.
يَقُومَ — root ق و م. Yaqūma is to rise and go. Once you are on your feet, the moment has passed.
سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ
Subḥānaka-llāhumma wa-bi-ḥamdik
It opens by clearing Allāh of every fault and giving Him praise.
سُبْحَانَكَ — root س ب ح. Subḥānaka addresses Allāh directly, unlike subḥāna-llāh. The talk was your own, so the apology is face to face.
أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
ashhadu an lā ilāha illā ant
Then testimony is given: worship belongs to You and to no one else.
أَشْهَدُ — root ش ه د. A shahādah is testimony a person stakes himself on, not an opinion he reports.
أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ، وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ
astaghfiruk, wa-atūbu ilayk
Two things together: ask for the past to be covered, and turn back from it.
وَأَتُوبُ — root ت و ب. Tawbah is turning round and coming back. Forgiveness is asked for; the returning is done.
إِلَّا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا كَانَ فِي مَجْلِسِهِ ذَلِكَ
illā ghufira lahu mā kāna fī majlisihi dhālik
Whatever was said in that sitting is wiped off him.
غُفِرَ — root غ ف ر. Ghufira is passive: it was forgiven, by Allāh. Ghafara is to cover a thing over.

لَغَطُهُالمُرَادُ: الكَلَامُ الَّذِي لَا يَنْفَعُ
laghaṭuhu — his clamourWhat is meant: speech that brings no benefit.

Chapter 75 — Sincerity to Allāh

Book p.170 · حَقُّ اللَّهِ ﷻ — The Right of Allāh · 2 entries in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«قَالَ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: أَنَا أَغْنَى الشُّرَكَاءِ عَنِ الشِّرْكِ، مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلاً أَشْرَكَ فِيهِ مَعِي غَيْرِي؛ تَرَكْتُهُ وَشِرْكَهُ»

✎Added by us

“Allāh, blessed and exalted, said: ‘Of all who are given a partner, I am the one with least need of a partner. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I leave him and his association.’”

EstablishesA deed done partly for someone other than Allāh is left to that other, and lost.

Qāla-llāhu tabāraka wa-taʿālā: Anā aghna-sh-shurakāʾi ʿani-sh-shirk, man ʿamila ʿamalan ashraka fīhi maʿī ghayrī; taraktuhu wa-shirkah

قَالَsaid
اللَّهُAllāh
تَبَارَكَblessed is He
وَتَعَالَىand exalted
أَنَاI am
أَغْنَىthe least in need
الشُّرَكَاءِof partners
عَنِfor
الشِّرْكِa partner
مَنْwhoever
عَمِلَdoes
عَمَلاًa deed
أَشْرَكَhe associates
فِيهِin it
مَعِيwith Me
غَيْرِيsomeone other than Me
تَرَكْتُهُI leave him
وَشِرْكَهُand his association
قَالَ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى
Qāla-llāhu tabāraka wa-taʿālā
What follows is Allāh's own speech, reported to us by the Prophet ﷺ.
تَبَارَكَ — root ب ر ك. Tabāraka: His blessing is His own and abundant, not something received from anyone.
أَنَا أَغْنَى الشُّرَكَاءِ عَنِ الشِّرْكِ
Anā aghna-sh-shurakāʾi ʿani-sh-shirk
Of everyone who might be given a share in something, Allāh has the least use for a co-owner.
أَغْنَى — root غ ن ي. Ghinā is having no need at all. The superlative aghnā puts Him beyond need entirely.
مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلاً أَشْرَكَ فِيهِ مَعِي غَيْرِي
man ʿamila ʿamalan ashraka fīhi maʿī ghayrī
The case is a deed done for Allāh and for somebody else at the same time.
أَشْرَكَ — root ش ر ك, Form IV. To bring in a partner. The deed is not swapped for another, only shared, and sharing is enough.
تَرَكْتُهُ وَشِرْكَهُ
taraktuhu wa-shirkah
Allāh does not take His portion. He leaves the whole thing to the other party.
تَرَكْتُهُ — root ت ر ك. Taraka is to leave a thing where it lies and walk away. The deed goes unrewarded.

رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌReported by Muslim

٢
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، إِيَّاكُمْ وَشِرْكَ السَّرَائِرِ. قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، وَمَا شِرْكُ السَّرَائِرِ؟ قَالَ: يَقُومُ الرَّجُلُ فَيُصَلِّي، فَيُزَيِّنُ صَلَاتَهُ جَاهِداً لِمَا يَرَى مِنْ نَظَرِ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ، فَذَلِكَ شِرْكُ السَّرَائِرِ»

✎Added by us

“O people, beware of the association hidden inside you. They said, ‘Messenger of Allāh, what is the association hidden inside us?’ He said, ‘A man stands and prays, and takes pains over the beauty of his prayer because of the people's eyes he sees upon him. That is the association hidden inside.’”

EstablishesMaking worship look better because people are watching is hidden shirk, even when the act itself is correct.

Ayyuha-n-nās, iyyākum wa-shirka-s-sarāʾir. Qālū: Yā Rasūla-llāh, wa-mā shirku-s-sarāʾir? Qāla: Yaqūmu-r-rajulu fa-yuṣallī, fa-yuzayyinu ṣalātahu jāhidan limā yarā min naẓari-n-nāsi ilayh, fa-dhālika shirku-s-sarāʾir

أَيُّهَا النَّاسُO people
إِيَّاكُمْbeware
وَشِرْكَ السَّرَائِرِthe association of inner secrets
قَالُواthey said
يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِO Messenger of Allāh
وَمَاand what is
شِرْكُ السَّرَائِرِthe association of inner secrets
قَالَhe said
يَقُومُstands up
الرَّجُلُthe man
فَيُصَلِّيand prays
فَيُزَيِّنُand adorns
صَلَاتَهُhis prayer
جَاهِداًstriving hard
لِمَاbecause of what
يَرَىhe sees
مِنْof
نَظَرِ النَّاسِthe people's looking
إِلَيْهِat him
فَذَلِكَso that is
شِرْكُ السَّرَائِرِthe association of inner secrets
أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، إِيَّاكُمْ وَشِرْكَ السَّرَائِرِ
Ayyuha-n-nās, iyyākum wa-shirka-s-sarāʾir
A public warning, and the danger named is one nobody can see from outside.
السَّرَائِرِ — root س ر ر. Sarāʾir is the plural of sarīrah: the inner secrets, what a person keeps inside himself.
قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، وَمَا شِرْكُ السَّرَائِرِ
Qālū: Yā Rasūla-llāh, wa-mā shirku-s-sarāʾir?
The Companions do not recognise the term, so they ask for it plainly.
قَالُوا — root ق و ل. Their question is kept in the hadith, which is how the definition reached us.
قَالَ: يَقُومُ الرَّجُلُ فَيُصَلِّي، فَيُزَيِّنُ صَلَاتَهُ جَاهِداً
Qāla: Yaqūmu-r-rajulu fa-yuṣallī, fa-yuzayyinu ṣalātahu jāhidan
The example is a man at prayer, working at how the prayer looks.
فَيُزَيِّنُ — root ز ي ن, Form II. To adorn. The prayer comes out better, and that is exactly where the problem sits.
لِمَا يَرَى مِنْ نَظَرِ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ
limā yarā min naẓari-n-nāsi ilayh
What drives the effort is the eyes on him, not the One he is standing before.
نَظَرِ — root ن ظ ر. Naẓar is a look or gaze. Being watched is the cause, and the cause is what is judged.
فَذَلِكَ شِرْكُ السَّرَائِرِ
fa-dhālika shirku-s-sarāʾir
That is the thing being named: worship shared with an audience.
شِرْكُ — root ش ر ك. Shirk here is not idol worship but a divided motive inside an act that looks sound.

Chapter 76 — Mindfulness of Allāh

Book p.172 · حَقُّ اللَّهِ ﷻ — The Right of Allāh · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ»

✎Added by us

“Fear Allāh wherever you are. Follow a bad deed with a good one, and it will wipe it out. And deal with people with good character.”

EstablishesTaqwā holds in every place, bad deeds are answered with good ones, and people are met with good character.

Ittaqi-llāha ḥaythumā kunt, wa-atbiʿi-s-sayyiʾata-l-ḥasanata tamḥuhā, wa-khāliqi-n-nāsa bi-khuluqin ḥasan

اتَّقِfear / guard against
اللَّهَAllāh
حَيْثُمَاwherever
كُنْتَyou are
وَأَتْبِعِand follow
السَّيِّئَةَthe bad deed
الحَسَنَةَwith the good deed
تَمْحُهَاit wipes it out
وَخَالِقِand deal with
النَّاسَpeople
بِخُلُقٍwith character
حَسَنٍthat is good
اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ
Ittaqi-llāha ḥaythumā kunt
Taqwā is not tied to a place. It travels with you.
اتَّقِ — root و ق ي. Taqwā is putting a guard between yourself and what harms you. The command is to keep that guard up everywhere.
وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا
wa-atbiʿi-s-sayyiʾata-l-ḥasanata tamḥuhā
When you slip, put a good deed straight behind it, and the good one erases it.
تَمْحُهَا — root م ح و. Maḥā is to rub out writing. The erasing is done by the good deed, not by time passing.
وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
wa-khāliqi-n-nāsa bi-khuluqin ḥasan
The third command turns outward: meet people well.
بِخُلُقٍ — root خ ل ق. The book glosses the phrase: use good character with them. Khuluq is a settled disposition, not a passing mood.
الكِتَابFrom the book
مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الكِتَابThe author's own footnote glosses
بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍأَيِ: اسْتَعْمِلِ الخُلُقَ الحَسَنَ مَعَهُمْ
bi-khuluqin ḥasan — with good characterThat is: employ good character with them.

Chapter 77 — Supplication

Book p.173 · حَقُّ اللَّهِ ﷻ — The Right of Allāh · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«يُسْتَجَابُ لِأَحَدِكُمْ مَا لَمْ يَعْجَلْ، يَقُولُ: دَعَوْتُ، فَلَمْ يُسْتَجَبْ لِي»

✎Added by us

“One of you is answered as long as he does not grow hasty and say, ‘I prayed, and I was not answered.’”

EstablishesDuʿāʾ keeps being answered as long as the one asking does not give up and declare it refused.

Yustajābu li-aḥadikum mā lam yaʿjal, yaqūlu: Daʿawtu, fa-lam yustajab lī

يُسْتَجَابُis answered
لِأَحَدِكُمْfor one of you
مَاas long as
لَمْnot
يَعْجَلْhe hastens
يَقُولُsaying
دَعَوْتُI prayed
فَلَمْand it was not
يُسْتَجَبْanswered
لِيfor me
يُسْتَجَابُ لِأَحَدِكُمْ
Yustajābu li-aḥadikum
The answer is the normal case, and that is where the hadith begins.
يُسْتَجَابُ — root ج و ب, Form X passive. It is answered for him. The passive leaves the Answerer understood without naming Him.
مَا لَمْ يَعْجَلْ
mā lam yaʿjal
One condition only: do not run out of patience.
يَعْجَلْ — root ع ج ل. ʿAjila is to want a thing before its time. It is the haste that cuts the answer off, not the asking.
يَقُولُ: دَعَوْتُ، فَلَمْ يُسْتَجَبْ لِي
yaqūlu: Daʿawtu, fa-lam yustajab lī
The haste is defined by a sentence a man says about his own duʿāʾ.
دَعَوْتُ — root د ع و. Daʿawtu is past tense: I called. Putting it that way closes a file Allāh has not closed.

مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِAgreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim)

Chapter 78 — Making Images

Book p.174 · حَقُّ اللَّهِ ﷻ — The Right of Allāh · 2 entries in the printed text.

١
عَنْ أَبِي جُحَيْفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَAbū Juḥayfah (may Allāh be pleased with him) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«لَعَنَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ المُصَوِّرَ»

✎Added by us

Abū Juḥayfah (may Allāh be pleased with him) said: “The Prophet ﷺ cursed the maker of images.”

EstablishesMaking images of living things is not a small matter; the Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who does it.

Laʿana-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ al-muṣawwir

لَعَنَcursed
النَّبِيُّ ﷺthe Prophet ﷺ
المُصَوِّرَthe image-maker
لَعَنَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ
Laʿana-n-Nabiyyu ﷺ
The Prophet ﷺ himself pronounced it, and what he pronounced was a curse.
لَعَنَ — root ل ع ن. A laʿnah is being driven away from mercy. The word is reserved for grave matters.
المُصَوِّرَ
al-muṣawwir
The one cursed is identified by his craft, not by a single act.
المُصَوِّرَ — root ص و ر, Form II active participle. Muṣawwir is one who forms images. Al-Muṣawwir, the Fashioner, is also a name of Allāh.

رَوَاهُ البُخَارِيُّReported by al-Bukhārī

٢
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كُلُّ مُصَوِّرٍ فِي النَّارِ، يَجْعَلُ لَهُ بِكُلِّ صُورَةٍ صَوَّرَهَا نَفْساً فَتُعَذِّبُهُ فِي جَهَنَّمَ»

✎Added by us

“Every image-maker is in the Fire. For every image he made, Allāh gives it a soul, and it torments him in Hell.”

EstablishesThe image-maker's own images become his punishment, each one given a soul to torment him.

Kullu muṣawwirin fī-n-nār, yajʿalu lahu bi-kulli ṣūratin ṣawwarahā nafsan fa-tuʿadhdhibuhu fī Jahannam

كُلُّevery
مُصَوِّرٍimage-maker
فِيis in
النَّارِthe Fire
يَجْعَلُHe gives
لَهُfor him

كُلُّ مُصَوِّرٍ فِي النَّارِ
Kullu muṣawwirin fī-n-nār
The verdict is given first, flat and without exception, then explained.
كُلُّ — root ك ل ل. Kull followed by a singular indefinite noun means every single one, with no case left out.
يَجْعَلُ لَهُ بِكُلِّ صُورَةٍ صَوَّرَهَا نَفْساً
yajʿalu lahu bi-kulli ṣūratin ṣawwarahā nafsan
For each image he made, a soul is put into it.
يَجْعَلُ — root ج ع ل. The book supplies the missing subject: Allāh. He is the one who gives the soul.
فَتُعَذِّبُهُ فِي جَهَنَّمَ

What he made turns round on him.
فَتُعَذِّبُهُ — root ع ذ ب, Form II. The verb is feminine because the image is the one doing the tormenting.

Chapter 79 — Keeping Up With the Qurʾān

Book p.176 · عِبَادَاتٌ — Acts of Worship · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said

«تَعَاهَدُوا هَذَا القُرْآنَ؛ فَوَالَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ، لَهُوَ أَشَدُّ تَفَلُّتاً مِنَ الإِبِلِ فِي عُقُلِهَا»

Taʿāhadū hādha-l-Qurʾān
The command is to keep coming back to it, not to visit it once.
تَعَاهَدُوا — root ع ه د, Form VI. The book glosses it: stay at it steadily, reciting and memorising. A ʿahd is a standing commitment.
فَوَالَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ
fa-wa-lladhī nafsu Muḥammadin bi-yadih
An oath, and he swears it on the One who holds his own life.
بِيَدِهِ — root ي د. The oath is a heavy one, which tells you the warning attached to it is not light.
لَهُوَ أَشَدُّ تَفَلُّتاً
la-huwa ashaddu tafallutan
Memorised Qurʾān does not sit still. It works its way out.
تَفَلُّتاً — root ف ل ت, Form V. Tafallut is breaking loose and getting away. What escapes was being held before.
مِنَ الإِبِلِ فِي عُقُلِهَا
mina-l-ibili fī ʿuqulihā
The comparison is a camel already roped, which still finds a way out.
عُقُلِهَا — root ع ق ل. The book explains: ʿuqul is the plural of ʿiqāl, a rope. Even tied, the camel goes.

Chapter 80 — The Obligation of the Congregational Prayer

Book p.177 · عِبَادَاتٌ — Acts of Worship · 1 entry in the printed text.

١
وُجُوبُ صَلَاةِ الجَمَاعَةِḤadīth
الكِتَابFrom the book

أَتَى النَّبِيَّ ﷺ رَجُلٌ أَعْمَى فَقَالَ: «يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ لِي قَائِدٌ يَقُودُنِي إِلَى المَسْجِدِ. فَسَأَلَ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ أَنْ يُرَخِّصَ لَهُ، فَيُصَلِّيَ فِي بَيْتِهِ؛ فَرَخَّصَ لَهُ. فَلَمَّا وَلَّى، دَعَاهُ، فَقَالَ: هَلْ تَسْمَعُ النِّدَاءَ بِالصَّلَاةِ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: فَأَجِبْ»

✎Added by us

A blind man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Messenger of Allāh, I have no guide to lead me to the masjid.” He asked the Prophet ﷺ to excuse him, so that he might pray in his house, and he excused him. Then, when the man had turned to go, he called him back and said, “Do you hear the call to prayer?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Then answer it.”

EstablishesHearing the adhān calls a man to the congregation, even when he is blind and has no guide.

Atā-n-Nabiyya ﷺ rajulun aʿmā fa-qāla: Yā Rasūla-llāh, innahu laysa lī qāʾidun yaqūdunī ilā-l-masjid. Fa-saʾala-n-Nabiyya ﷺ an yurakhkhiṣa lah, fa-yuṣalliya fī baytih; fa-rakhkhaṣa lah. Fa-lammā wallā, daʿāh, fa-qāla: Hal tasmaʿu-n-nidāʾa bi-ṣ-ṣalāh? Qāla: Naʿam, qāla: Fa-ajib

Atā-n-Nabiyya ﷺ rajulun aʿmā fa-qāla
A blind man comes to him, and the difficulty is put by the man himself.
أَعْمَى — root ع م ي. Aʿmā is blind. His condition stays in view for the whole hadith.
يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ لِي قَائِدٌ يَقُودُنِي إِلَى المَسْجِدِ
Yā Rasūla-llāh, innahu laysa lī qāʾidun yaqūdunī ilā-l-masjid
He has nobody to walk him there, so the excuse is a genuine one.
قَائِدٌ — root ق و د. A qāʾid leads someone by the hand. He is describing a lack of help, not a lack of will.
فَسَأَلَ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ أَنْ يُرَخِّصَ لَهُ، فَيُصَلِّيَ فِي بَيْتِهِ؛ فَرَخَّصَ لَهُ
Fa-saʾala-n-Nabiyya ﷺ an yurakhkhiṣa lah, fa-yuṣalliya fī baytih; fa-rakhkhaṣa lah
He asks to be let off and pray at home, and permission is granted.
يُرَخِّصَ — root ر خ ص. The book glosses it: to give leave. A rukhṣah is a concession from the standing rule.
فَلَمَّا وَلَّى، دَعَاهُ، فَقَالَ
Fa-lammā wallā, daʿāh, fa-qāla
The permission is taken back before the man is out of the room.
وَلَّى — root و ل ي. The book glosses it: he turned and left. The Prophet ﷺ calls after him at once.
هَلْ تَسْمَعُ النِّدَاءَ بِالصَّلَاةِ
Hal tasmaʿu-n-nidāʾa bi-ṣ-ṣalāh?
One question settles it: can you hear the adhān?
النِّدَاءَ — root ن د و. Nidāʾ is the call, the adhān. Hearing it is the test, not the distance or the difficulty.
قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: فَأَجِبْ
Qāla: Naʿam, qāla: Fa-ajib
He can hear it, so he is told to answer it.
فَأَجِبْ — root ج و ب. Ajib is a command: respond. The adhān is treated as a summons that expects a reply.

وَلَّىأَيِ: انْصَرَفَ
wallā — he turned awayThat is: he departed.

✎Added by us

“When you come to the prayer, calm is what is owed from you.”

أَتَيْتُمُ — root أ ت ي. Atā is simply to come. So the instruction is about the journey there.

Chapter 82 — Some of the Rights of the Prophet ﷺ

Book p.180 · حَقُّ المَخْلُوقِينَ — Rights of Creation · 5 entries in the printed text.

١
قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«كُلُّ أُمَّتِي يَدْخُلُونَ الجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَبَى. قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، وَمَنْ يَأْبَى؟! قَالَ: مَنْ أَطَاعَنِي دَخَلَ الجَنَّةَ، وَمَنْ عَصَانِي فَقَدْ أَبَى»

✎Added by us

“All of my nation will enter Paradise except the one who refuses. They said, ‘Messenger of Allāh, who would refuse?’ He said, ‘Whoever obeys me enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused.’”

EstablishesObeying the Prophet ﷺ is the way into Paradise; disobeying him counts as refusing to enter.

Kullu ummatī yadkhulūna-l-jannata illā man abā
Everyone is included, and only one kind of person is left outside.
أَبَى — root أ ب ي. Abā is to refuse outright, not merely to fall short. The exception is a choice a person makes.
قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، وَمَنْ يَأْبَى
Qālū: Yā Rasūla-llāh, wa-man yaʾbā?
The Companions cannot picture anyone turning Paradise down.
يَأْبَى — root أ ب ي. Present tense: who is refusing, now? Their question is what makes room for the answer.
قَالَ: مَنْ أَطَاعَنِي دَخَلَ الجَنَّةَ
Qāla: Man aṭāʿanī dakhala-l-jannah
Obedience to him is named as the way in.
أَطَاعَنِي — root ط و ع, Form IV. Ṭāʿah is compliance given willingly. The object here is 'me': his own instruction.
وَمَنْ عَصَانِي فَقَدْ أَبَى
wa-man ʿaṣānī fa-qad abā
Disobedience is not treated as weakness here. It is counted as refusal.
عَصَانِي — root ع ص ي. ʿAṣā is to disobey an order you have received. The verdict is put in the past: fa-qad abā, he has already refused.

«لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى أَكُونَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ وَالِدِهِ وَوَلَدِهِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ»

“None of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child, and all people.”

«مَنْ أَحَقُّ النَّاسِ بِحُسْنِ صَحَابَتِي؟ قَالَ: أُمُّكَ. قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَنْ؟ قَالَ: ثُمَّ أُمُّكَ. قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَنْ؟ قَالَ: ثُمَّ أُمُّكَ. قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَنْ؟ قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَبُوكَ»

✎Added by us

A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Who among people has the most right to my good company?” He said: “Your mother.” He said: “Then who?” He said: “Then your mother.” He said: “Then who?” He said: “Then your mother.” He said: “Then who?” He said: “Then your father.”

EstablishesThe mother holds the first claim to good company, named three times over, and the father comes after her.

The man asks who has the strongest claim on his good treatment.
أَحَقُّ — root ح ق ق. Aḥaqq means most entitled, the one with the strongest ḥaqq or right. The question is about priority, not about who deserves kindness at all.

Qāla: Ummuk
The first answer is the mother.
أُمُّكَ — root أ م م. Umm is mother. The answer is one word, with no qualification attached to it.
قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَنْ؟ قَالَ: ثُمَّ أُمُّكَ
Qāla: Thumma man? Qāla: Thumma ummuk
He asks again, and gets the same answer.
ثُمَّ — Thumma orders what follows after what came before. Here it invites a second name, and the same name is given.
قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَنْ؟ قَالَ: ثُمَّ أُمُّكَ
Qāla: Thumma man? Qāla: Thumma ummuk
A third time, and still the mother.
مَنْ — Man is the question word for a person. Repeating it three times is what makes the weight of the answer land.
قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَنْ؟ قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَبُوكَ
Qāla: Thumma man? Qāla: Thumma abūk
Only on the fourth asking is the father named.
أَبُوكَ — root أ ب و. Ab is father. He is not left out, but he is placed after three turns given to the mother.

The answer is one word: the fruit of Paradise, gathered.
جَنَاهَا — root ج ن ي. Janā is fruit taken from the tree. The book explains that the visitor, in the reward he collects, is like a man among the palms of Paradise picking its fruit.

«خَمْسٌ مِنَ الفِطْرَةِ: الخِتَانُ، وَالِاسْتِحْدَادُ، وَتَقْلِيمُ الأَظْفَارِ، وَنَتْفُ الإِبْطِ، وَقَصُّ الشَّارِبِ»

✎Added by us

“Five things are of the natural disposition: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the nails, plucking the underarm hair, and clipping the moustache.”

EstablishesFive acts of personal grooming belong to sound human nature and are to be kept up.

Khamsun mina-l-fiṭrah: al-khitānu, wa-l-istiḥdādu, wa taqlīmu-l-aẓfāri, wa natfu-l-ibṭi, wa qaṣṣu-sh-shārib

These five are not custom; they belong to how a person is made.
الفِطْرَةِ — root ف ط ر. The book explains fiṭrah as what people were formed upon. These acts suit the human make-up itself.
الخِتَانُ، وَالِاسْتِحْدَادُ

The first two concern the body's private care.
وَالِاسْتِحْدَادُ — root ح د د, from ḥadīd, iron. The book explains istiḥdād as shaving the pubic hair; the word is taken from the blade used for it.
وَتَقْلِيمُ الأَظْفَارِ، وَنَتْفُ الإِبْطِ، وَقَصُّ الشَّارِبِ
wa taqlīmu-l-aẓfāri, wa natfu-l-ibṭi, wa qaṣṣu-sh-shārib
Nails, underarm and moustache complete the list.
وَنَتْفُ — root ن ت ف. Natf is pulling out by the root, while qaṣṣ is cutting back. Each act is named with the method that fits it.

٢
قَالَ أَنَسٌ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُAnas (may Allāh be pleased with him) said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«وُقِّتَ لَنَا فِي: قَصِّ الشَّارِبِ، وَتَقْلِيمِ الأَظْفَارِ، وَنَتْفِ الإِبْطِ، وَحَلْقِ العَانَةِ؛ أَنْ لَا نَتْرُكَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً»

✎Added by us

Anas, may Allāh be pleased with him, said: “A time was set for us regarding clipping the moustache, trimming the nails, plucking the underarm hair and shaving the pubic hair: that we should not leave it longer than forty nights.”

EstablishesThese four grooming acts have an outer limit: they are not left longer than forty nights.

قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺThe Prophet ﷺ said
الكِتَابFrom the book

«السِّوَاكُ مَطْهَرَةٌ لِلْفَمِ، مَرْضَاةٌ لِلرَّبِّ»

✎Added by us

“The tooth-stick is a means of cleansing for the mouth and a means of pleasing the Lord.”

EstablishesUsing the siwāk cleans the mouth and pleases Allāh, so hygiene and worship meet in one act.

As-siwāku maṭharatun li-l-fam, marḍātun li-r-Rabb

السِّوَاكُthe tooth-stick
مَطْهَرَةٌa means of cleansing
لِلْفَمِfor the mouth

السِّوَاكُ مَطْهَرَةٌ لِلْفَمِ

The first result is plain physical cleanliness.
مَطْهَرَةٌ — root ط ه ر. The pattern mafʿalah names the means or instrument. The siwāk is the tool by which the mouth is made clean.
مَرْضَاةٌ لِلرَّبِّ
marḍātun li-r-Rabb
The same small act also earns Allāh's pleasure.
مَرْضَاةٌ — root ر ض ي. The same pattern again: a means of gaining riḍā. The parallel wording ties a light habit to a heavy reward.

رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُReported by Aḥmad
